Using Bayesian analyses of the binary-neutron-star events GW170817 and GW190425, we obtain a combined constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling of $a\lesssim6.2\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}^2$ at $90\%$ credibility, corresponding to a lower bound on the scalar mass of $m_s\gtrsim3.2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. This constitutes the strongest astrophysical constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling, improving the previous best bound by approximately five orders of magnitude and demonstrating the sensitivity of binary-neutron-star inspirals to finite-range scalar interactions in the strong-field regime.

papers.title_en: Correlated Signatures of Plasma Lensing in Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract_en: Plasma lensing has been proposed to explain narrow spectra, multiple burst copies, frequency drifts, interference fringes, and polarization changes in fast radio bursts (FRBs). Because many of these features are not unique to lensing, a convincing identification requires several correlated observables to be reproduced by one lens model. We derive such relations for a one-dimensional Gaussian plasma lens near a fold caustic. We distinguish the phase separation of the merging images from their observable group-delay difference and identify three regimes: resolved burst copies, overlapping images with negligible mutual coherence, and coherent spectral interference. We connect the magnification, image delay, spectral-envelope width, fringe spacing, differential dispersion, time-frequency caustic curvature, and the brightness and ordering of the third image. We derive separate finite-source constraints from large fold magnification and from fringe visibility, and relate the wave-optics magnification scale to the plasma column of the lens. High-contrast fringes simultaneously constrain the source size and the mutual coherence of the two image fields, which constrains the intrinsic coherence of the FRB radiation once the observed spectrum and instrumental bandpass are accounted for. We also derive the conditions for differential Faraday rotation in magnetized lenses. Finally, we show that clean lensing by a volume-filling turbulent screen requires fine tuning between rare strong fluctuations and caustic confusion, suggesting that sparse sheets, filaments, interfaces, or shocked clumps are more promising lensing structures.

papers.title_en: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
papers.abstract_en: The near-field gravitational interaction between masses is always thought of as instantaneous, an assumption experimentally tested only up to 1.7 kHz, where measurements yield a bounds at the $10^{-5}$ s level. We propose a near-field experiment reaching up to megahertz frequencies, in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque. Because the detector rotor acts as a mechanical local oscillator, the megahertz signal is downconverted to a convenient band of a few hertz, and since at fixed geometry neither the torque nor the integration time depends on the rotation rate, higher frequencies are reached at no cost in sensitivity. With parameters within reach of magnetically levitated NdFeB rotors, a signal at 2 MHz yields a torque of $2\cdot 10^{-25}$ Nm, detectable in under an hour at 10 mK. Treating a possible departure from instantaneous gravitational coupling through a field relaxation time, the measured torque could constrain it at the $10^{-8}$ s level, improving on the existing bounds by more than three orders of magnitude. As a byproduct of our analysis, we derive the sensitivity of a rotor operated as a tunable high-frequency gravitational-wave detector, finding that a noise-equivalent strain around $10^{-22}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ could be achievable in the megahertz band.

papers.title_en: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ via $^{139}$La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the $Am2m$ Structure
papers.abstract_en: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.

papers.title_en: Tree tensor network states represent low-energy states faithfully
papers.abstract_en: Extending corresponding results for matrix product states [Verstraete and Cirac, PRB 73, 094423 (2006); Schuch et al. PRL 100, 030504 (2008)], it is shown how the approximation error of tree tensor network states (TTNS) can be bounded using Schmidt spectra or Rényi entanglement entropies of the target quantum state. Conversely, one obtains bounds on TTNS bond dimensions needed to achieve a specific approximation accuracy. The result implies that efficient TTNS approximations exist if $α<1$ Rényi entanglement entropies for single-branch cuts obey an area law, as in ground and low-energy states of certain gapped systems on tree graphs.

papers.title_en: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
papers.abstract_en: Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

papers.title_en: Axial black hole perturbations in purely-metric Horndeski theories
papers.abstract_en: We study axial (odd-parity) perturbations about static and spherically-symmetric curvaturised black hole solutions of purely-metric Horndeski theories. We first review the construction of purely-metric theories of gravity with second-order equations of motion and an additional propagating scalar degree of freedom which is purely gravitational. We then revisit the formation, in a subclass of these theories, of a new branch of hairy black hole solutions under tachyonic instabilities of the scalar field near the Schwarzschild solution. Because a non-zero Ricci curvature grows and by analogy with black hole scalarisation, the latter black hole formation mechanism is dubbed \emph{curvaturisation}. We then apply the first-order approach to the dynamics of axial perturbations and find that it is equivalent to that of axial perturbations in general relativity evolving in a distinct effective metric. We explicitly provide that effective metric in terms of the background and the Lagrangian functions, and show that it shares the same causality structure as the background metric of curvaturised black holes. By turning to the Schrödinger-like formulation of the perturbations, we analyse the scattering potential and conclude that the axial perturbations of curvaturised black holes are linearly stable. Finally, we confirm these findings by explicitly computing the fundamental quasi-normal mode as well as the first five overtones for the quadrupole $\ell = 2$.

papers.title_en: Magnetohydrodynamics During Reheating
papers.abstract_en: Reheating is a crucial phase that connects inflation with the hot Big Bang Universe. During this phase, the nonlinear interactions among the inflaton, the radiation plasma, and the primordial magnetic fields can influence the subsequent evolution of cosmic structures we observe today. In this paper, we develop a multifluid framework to investigate the evolution of three dimensional nonlinear magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) during the non instantaneous reheating phase driven by the perturbative decay of the inflaton into the radiation plasma. For the present paper, we consider the simplest scenario where the inflaton field homogeneously injects energy into the radiation sector. We study the MHD evolution of the coupled inflaton radiation system during the reheating phase, including the evolution of their individual kinetic energies, the velocity perturbations, vorticity, magnetic fields, and gravitational waves. We find that homogeneous energy transfer from the inflaton to the radiation sector increases the radiation and kinetic energy densities but does not significantly amplify the initial magnetic field perturbations. Consequently, the magnetic spectrum remains largely unchanged with respect to the instantaneous reheating scenario, while the velocity perturbations undergo a scale redistribution that affects the resulting GW spectrum. Our results demonstrate the importance of nonlinear multifluid MHD dynamics in understanding the evolution of primordial fields during reheating and provide a framework for exploring more realistic scenarios involving inhomogeneous decay processes and detailed thermalization effects.

papers.title_en: Density Modulations of Zero Sound
papers.abstract_en: We study the density modulation of an interacting Fermi gas caused by the uniform motion of an impurity at zero temperature. For strong enough interaction among Fermi atoms, the modulation propagates thanks to the excitation of the collective zero sound mode if the impurity speed is above the zero sound threshold. We are able to assess, via a semi-analytic evaluation, the extent of the zero sound contribution to the density oscillation over and above the incoherent background of particle-hole excitations. Given the strong dependence of the results on the features of the gas interaction potential, we also analyze how they vary depending on its strength, range and shape.

papers.title_en: Quantum JT Gravity in a box as a Pöschl-Teller Scattering Problem
papers.abstract_en: We present a canonical quantization of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity with finite Dirichlet boundary conditions, using the geodesic length between the two boundaries and its conjugate momentum as reduced phase space variables. The dynamics is recast as the scattering problem of a nonrelativistic particle in a repulsive Pöschl-Teller potential, naturally embedded within a hyperbolic reduction of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Casimir. We obtain exact wavefunctions of the universe and the disk partition function, interpreted as a transition matrix element between states of vanishing bare length. In the asymptotic limit, the theory reduces to Liouville quantum mechanics and reproduces the standard Schwarzian spectral density. At finite cutoff, however, the spectral measure exhibits genuinely nonperturbative corrections, absent in existing $T\bar T$ approaches. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of pinched disk geometries and are responsible for a controlled violation of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation. We also obtain closed form expressions for thermal two-point functions in terms of Wilson functions and propose diagrammatic rules for time- and out-of-time-ordered four-point functions. We further address the issue of the branch cut singularity of the quasi-local energy and propose a UV completion of the model in which the Brown-York charge is extended beyond the black hole horizon. This extension naturally generalizes the scattering problem to configurations that foliate the black hole interior.

papers.title_en: Anomaly effective actions for 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories
papers.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive analysis of the Wess-Zumino anomaly effective action of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories in components. After reviewing the coset construction of the Wess-Zumino action in the presence of an unbroken subgroup, the gauging of the conformal algebra and the Wess-Zumino effective action for non-supersymmetric conformal field theories with a U(1) symmetry in two and four dimensions, we revisit the superconformal anomalies of $\mathcal{N}=1$ conformal supergravity. Solving the Wess-Zumino consistency conditions we determine both the bosonic and fermionic superconformal anomalies in a two-parameter family of schemes, to quadratic order in the gravitino. Turning on a chiral compensator multiplet and identifying a local super-Poincaré subalgebra of the conformal supergravity algebra without gauge-fixing the coset symmetries, we employ the coset construction and the superconformal anomalies in order to evaluate the Wess-Zumino action for generic $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories coupled to conformal supergravity. By construction, this action reproduces the Weyl, R-symmetry, and S-supersymmetry coset anomalies, but its transformation under the unbroken Poincaré supersymmetry differs from the corresponding anomaly of the conformal supergravity functional. We show that there exists a local functional of the coset-invariant old-minimal fields that, when added to the Wess-Zumino action, results in a generalized Wess-Zumino action that reproduces all anomalies of the conformal supergravity functional. The same local functional enables us to determine the super-Weyl anomalies and the Wess-Zumino action of old-minimal supergravity, providing a component version of the known superspace Wess-Zumino action.

papers.title_en: Ising anyons in the $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory
papers.abstract_en: Ising anyons and $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory share the fusion rules and $F$-symbols, and their $R$-symbols agree up to braiding orientation and an overall phase. The quantum-group description, $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at $q = e^{iπ/4}$, is nevertheless not semisimple: tensor powers of the fundamental representation contain an additional spin-$3/2$ representation and reducible indecomposable representations, all of zero quantum dimension. We construct explicit highest-weight bases for up to four strands, compute the Racah and braiding matrices, and show that for four strands changes of fusion basis and braiding mix the physical sector with an indecomposable summand. We prove that this mixing affects neither the braid-closure invariant nor the plat-closure amplitude for any number of strands, so that each braiding matrix can be replaced by its physical block. The full representation theory thus reproduces the Ising-anyon data for all observables relevant to topological quantum computation.

papers.title_en: Exact Splitting of Amplitudes and One-Loop Integrands: A Classical Origin of Zeros
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a recursion based on hidden zeros that reconstructs complete tree level scattering amplitudes and one-loop integrands at generic kinematics. The recursion takes a universal exact-splitting form: both tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands are expressed as sums of products of complete tree functions, with the chosen zero conditions manifest in every term. We establish this structure for cubic scalar theory, the nonlinear sigma model, and inverse string Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) functions. We derive the tree splitting formula from the equations of motion, showing that hidden zeros arise when the product of two currents solves the equations of motion, while corrections away from the zero reconstruct the full amplitude. We further show that inverse KLT is the unique extension of $\mathrm{Tr}(φ^3)$ with higher-point non-derivative interactions that preserves hidden zeros.

papers.title_en: Quantum Tunneling-induced Hybridization and Coherent Dynamics of Jackiw-Rebbi Zero Modes in a Modified Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
papers.abstract_en: We investigate analytically and numerically the tunneling-induced hybridization and coherent dynamics of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes in a modified Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. Unlike the conventional SSH model, this modified system possess two bulk gap-closing points, namely the quadratic-type gap-closing point at momenta $k_0=0$ and the Dirac-type gap-closing points at $k_0=\pmπ/4a$. Although the quadratic point does not support a topological domain wall due to the absence of mass inversion, the low-energy Dirac theory around $k_0=\pmπ/4a$ predicts an effective mass that changes sign at two spatially separated domain walls under a kink profile, generating a pair of JR bound states with each states localized at one of those domain walls. We show that the finite spatial overlap between the JR zero modes lifts the zero-energy degeneracy through quantum tunneling, producing symmetric-antisymmetric hybridized states. Using an effective two-level description, we demonstrate that hybridized JR modes undergo coherent tunneling oscillations between the two domain walls, accompanied by periodic transfer of sublattice polarization between the (A,C) and (B,D) sectors. Our results establish a unified framework connecting JR zero modes, quantum tunneling, and coherent dynamics in modified SSH systems, offering a promising platform for controllable topological quantum-state transfer in engineered lattice structures.

papers.title_en: Hidden entropic order of emergent charges in a classical Ampère spin liquid
papers.abstract_en: Classical spin liquids are characterized by an extensive number of ground-state configurations. Coulomb spin liquids have, in this ground-state manifold, a divergence-free local constraint, which gives dipolar correlations and pinch points in the structure factor. Recently, models with a complementary ground-state constraint, defined by a zero-circulation constraint (Ampère's law), have been proposed. While classical Coulomb spin liquids forbid emergent charges, their Ampère counterparts leave the charges unconstrained. Here we study an Ising Ampère model on the octochlore lattice. The ground states obey a Gauss law for an antisymmetric rank-two field, i.e., three coupled two-dimensional Gauss laws, which are expected to produce pinch points in the structure factor. Nevertheless, maximal charges, vertices with all six arrows in or out, spontaneously accumulate on one of the two sublattices of the cubic lattice, with disordered signs. This order has a purely entropic origin; it washes out the pinch-point singularities at large scales, produces no magnetic Bragg peaks, and coexists with an extensive entropy. The system enters into this sublattice long-range ordered state through a continuous transition in what seems to be the three-dimensional Ising universality class. Moreover, the state has no magnetic order; it is even under time reversal: it is a hidden, entropic order within the Ampère manifold. Thus, a system whose Gauss law would predict an algebraic spin liquid becomes, through a non-magnetic ordering transition, a partially ordered short-range spin liquid. Our study is based on a combination of the constraint-vector theory, exact bounds and enumeration, and Monte Carlo, Wang-Landau, and parallel-tempering simulations.

papers.title_en: 5-brane webs and generalised symmetries
papers.abstract_en: 5-brane webs provide a powerful geometric description of five-dimensional quantum field theories, encoding data such as symmetries and dualities. Although the extraction of continuous 0-form symmetries from these systems is well understood, their higher-form symmetries have received less attention. We develop a microscopic prescription for determining 1-form symmetries directly from 5-brane webs. BPS Wilson lines are represented by configurations of D3-branes and $(p,q)$ strings, while their screening by local operators is realised through string junctions, Higgsing, and Hanany-Witten transitions. For webs without orientifold planes, this construction reproduces the Smith normal form prescription based on asymptotic 7-brane charges. We extend the analysis to webs containing O7- and O5- planes. For O7$^-$-planes, the resolved 7-brane charges can be incorporated into the Smith normal form, whereas for O7$^+$-planes we propose an effective charge prescription and test it in both Lagrangian and non-Lagrangian examples. For webs with O5-planes, configurations of half-D3-branes reproduce the centre symmetries of Spin gauge theories and their breaking by matter. Crucially, we find that the 1-form symmetry of an O5-plane system is not determined by asymptotic data alone, but can depend on the local structure of the brane configuration near the orientifold.

papers.title_en: Inside the cocoon: a comprehensive explanation of the spectra of Little Red Dots
papers.abstract_en: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has revealed a new population of compact galaxies, the `little red dots' (LRDs), whose nature remains unclear. We assemble grating spectra for 53 LRD-like objects and use self-consistent radiative-transfer calculations to show that a supermassive black hole embedded in a dense gas cocoon reproduces the spectra in detail, without requiring a stellar-like photosphere. The near-symmetric, electron-scattering-broadened emission line-shapes can be reproduced by cocoons with comparable inflowing and outflowing mass-fluxes. The same cocoon structure also simultaneously accounts for the continuum shapes, H and He line equivalent widths, and absorption features, and predicts metal-line absorption, X-ray weakness, and muted variability. We predict correlations should exist between Balmer break strength, Balmer line absorption, and scattering line width, and confirm their presence in the observed sample. Typical LRDs have black holes of order $10^{6}$ $\mathrm{M}_\odot$ inside ionised cocoons of tens of $\mathrm{M}_\odot$, likely fed by a much larger cold-gas reservoir.

papers.title_en: Cosmological Backreaction and the Separate Universe Conjecture: Dynamical volume partitioning of Newtonian cosmologies
papers.abstract_en: We provide a description of general Newtonian cosmologies for collisionless matter in terms of an exact and dynamical volume partitioning of global realizations of Newtonian models. Employing the formalism for the description of cosmological backreaction, an interaction between the inhomogeneities of the formation of structures in the Universe and their average properties can be analyzed. Our results can be regarded as a tool for many potential applications in the context of Newtonian simulations, but they also provide an exact way to assume analytical properties of the universe models on regional scales in conformity with global integral constraints on their average properties. We discuss approaches in relation to `separate Universe conjectures' in the literature and examine their consistency with the exact partitioning framework. In particular, using the Average Expansion Rate Approximation (AvERA) as an example, we show that identifying locally assigned Friedmannian rates with physical regional expansion rates is constrained by the global Newtonian 3-torus condition. Alternatively, when the simulation cells are interpreted as non-material control volumes, Reynolds transport introduces mass flux and flux-backreaction terms, so that their dynamics is not in general that of independent Friedmann domains. We also discuss the corresponding consistency conditions for stable clustering prescriptions.

papers.title_en: Constraining the white-dwarf mass in the intermediate polar IGR J17014-4306 using X-ray and optical spectroscopy
papers.abstract_en: Intermediate polars (IPs), a subclass of magnetic cataclysmic variables, often show discrepancies between white-dwarf (WD) mass measurements from X-ray spectral modeling and optical dynamical studies. We investigate the IP IGR J17014-4306. We performed a joint spectral analysis of NuSTAR observations combined with archival XMM-Newton and Swift data, modeling the broad-band X-ray spectrum with a multi-temperature cooling-flow model. Additionally, we obtained time-resolved optical spectroscopy with the SOAR telescope to measure the radial velocity of the donor star and constrain the system's orbital parameters. The X-ray spectral analysis reveals a very high post-shock plasma temperature of $kT_{\max}=50_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{keV}$, corresponding to a WD mass of $M_{\mathrm{WD}}=0.94_{-0.07}^{+0.09}\,M_\odot$. We also fitted the NuSTAR spectrum above 10 keV with the ipolar30KK model, obtaining $M_{\mathrm{WD}}=0.88_{-0.12}^{+0.14}\,M_\odot$. Our optical spectroscopy yields a radial-velocity semi-amplitude for the companion star of $K_2=165\pm4\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and an optical mass function of $f(M)=0.249\pm0.018\,M_\odot$. Combined with the eclipse geometry and the WD mass estimate from the X-ray models, these results favor a high mass ratio, $0.76\lesssim q\lesssim0.95$, and a donor-star mass of approximately $0.67\lesssim M_2/M_\odot\lesssim0.89$. In the limiting case of $q=1$, the WD mass has an upper limit of $1.14\,M_\odot$. Together with the X-ray measurements, this indicates a relatively massive WD. The lack of an independent measurement of the WD dynamical mass leaves it unclear whether the dynamical mass is consistent with the X-ray measurements or whether the X-ray mass is underestimated, as has been found for other IPs. Thus, our constraints make IGR J17014-4306 an important system for improving our understanding of IPs.

papers.title_en: Tachyonic Encore: A universal shift of inflationary observables
papers.abstract_en: We propose a generic mechanism applicable to single-field inflaton models in which a light axion spectator, initialized near the hilltop of its potential, reshapes inflationary observables through purely gravitational multi-field dynamics. During inflation the axion is frozen and the background follows an effectively single-field trajectory. After inflation ends, the axion rolls, inducing a turn in field space and transient tachyonic phases of the isocurvature mode. The resulting ``tachyonic encore'' occurs entirely on super-horizon scales. These phases generate a nearly scale-invariant enhancement of the curvature power spectrum, suppressing the tensor-to-scalar ratio and shifting the scalar tilt to a weighted combination of adiabatic and entropic tilts at horizon crossing. We show that these effects can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with current CMB constraints. The same dynamics predict local non-Gaussianity, $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc.}\sim \mathcal{O}(1)$, within reach of upcoming surveys.

papers.title_en: Entanglement Entropy in Non Relativistic Collisions
papers.abstract_en: We study numerically the build-up of entanglement entropy between two colliding, non relativistic particles, that are driven by the plain Schrödinger equation containing local, finite range potentials, and whose initial state is the product of two independent wave packets. Different situations are considered, ranging from a tunnel and mirror effect at low energy in front of a barrier, to higher energies, and also attraction rather than repulsion. While the calculated wave functions and density matrices significantly depend on the physical situations described by our models, the build-up trends and values in time of entanglement entropy look surprisingly alike one another.

papers.title_en: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge invariance
papers.abstract_en: The Kogut-Susskind (KS) formulation of gauge theories constructs quantum many-body Hamiltonians with gauge invariance under a compact Lie group exactly implemented on a spatial lattice. Here, we revisit this construction for a non-compact gauge group. Although motivated in part by theories like general relativity whose first-order formulation involves the non-compact Lorentz group as a local symmetry, we focus on simpler cases in one spatial dimension akin to the Schwinger model. In a bottom-up approach, we show how exact gauge invariance under the simplest non-compact Lie group ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be retained exactly on a 1D lattice, and highlight the differences that arise with respect to compact gauge groups, including a continuous spectrum of the Casimir operators of the gauge fields and the emergence of infinite-dimensional representations of the matter fields. For the pure gauge theory, we discuss how a consistent restriction to the positive semigroup ${\rm SL}^{+}(2,\mathbb{R})$ reproduces well-known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Motivated by the constraint structure of general dilaton gravity, we introduce static charges coupled to the non-compact gauge field, which can be realised by single-fermion degrees of freedom living in an additional, synthetic dimension. With static charges our lattice model remains exactly integrable, but when extending to dynamical fermionic matter, we arrive at an interacting 1D ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ KS gauge theory. We give an interpretation of this model as a chain of charges sequentially connected by strings whose tension pulls matter left or right depending on the sign of the relative continuous ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ fluxes. This picture becomes exact when the involved ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ charges are strongly self-interacting, where we solve the reduced two-body problem analytically.

papers.title_en: The two-flavor Schwinger model at 50: Solving Coleman's puzzles
papers.abstract_en: In his 1976 paper "More about the massive Schwinger model," Coleman introduced $1+1$-dimensional Quantum Electrodynamics coupled to two charged massive fermions. By applying Abelian bosonization, he elucidated much of the physics of this two-flavor Schwinger model, but he listed three puzzles at the end of his paper. We present new analytical and numerical calculations to solve Coleman's three puzzles and thereby deepen our understanding of this model. These puzzles pertain to the theory with equal fermion masses at $θ= 0$ and at $θ= π$, as well as the size of isospin-breaking effects when the fermion masses are unequal. For the puzzle at $θ= π$, the solution is related to the structure of the zero-temperature phase diagram arXiv:2305.04437: for equal fermion masses $m$, the model exhibits spontaneous breaking of charge conjugation symmetry and absence of confinement for any value of the gauge coupling $g$, so that there is a smooth interpolation from weak to strong coupling. Using two-loop Renormalization Group and integrability methods, we show that the mass gap behaves as $\sim m e^{-0.111 g^2/m^2}$ in the strong coupling regime $m\ll g$. Our numerical results using the lattice Hamiltonian are in good agreement with this behavior. For the puzzle at $θ= 0$, the solution is related to a level crossing between two isosinglet particles with different discrete quantum numbers; we demonstrate the necessity of such a crossing by comparing integrability and weak coupling calculations, and we also exhibit the crossing numerically. Finally, we provide a new estimate for the size of isospin-breaking effects caused by different fermion masses at strong coupling.

papers.title_en: Energetic Nonthermal Electrons within the Above-the-looptop Regions in Solar Flares: Acceleration, Feedback, and Quasi-Periodic Pulsations
papers.abstract_en: Solar flares are among the most dramatic events in the solar system, releasing substantial magnetic energy and accelerating a large number of electrons to high energies. Notably, in certain events, the above-the-looptop region may contain a significant population of nonthermal electrons, both in number and energy. For the first time, we adopt a novel numerical method that combines magnetohydrodynamics with energetic particles incorporating feedback from nonthermal electrons to investigate electron acceleration and transport in solar flares. We find that a large fraction of energetic electrons are accelerated via the current sheet and termination shock regions. Most energetic electrons are concentrated in the above-the-looptop region, carrying a sizable amount of the released energy. We observe that greater feedback of nonthermal electrons leads to steeper energy spectra. The energy density of the nonthermal electrons oscillates due to the periodic impact of magnetic islands into the above-the-looptop, which may help explain the observed quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs). Our simulations provide new insights into the origin of nonthermal electrons and associated emissions in the above-the-looptop region.

papers.title_en: Cost scaling of MPS and TTNS simulations for 2D and 3D systems with area-law entanglement
papers.abstract_en: Tensor network states are an indispensable tool for the simulation of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. In recent years, tree tensor network states (TTNS) have been successfully used for two-dimensional systems and to benchmark quantum simulation approaches for condensed matter, nuclear, and particle physics. In comparison to the more traditional approach based on matrix product states (MPS), the graph distance of physical degrees of freedom can be drastically reduced in TTNS. Surprisingly, it turns out that, for large systems in $D>1$ spatial dimensions, MPS simulations of low-energy states are nevertheless more efficient than TTNS simulations. With a focus on $D=2$ and 3, the scaling of computational costs for different boundary conditions is determined under the assumption that the system obeys an entanglement (log-)area law, implying that bond dimensions scale exponentially in the interface area of the associated subsystems.

papers.title_en: Inflationary attractors in metric-affine gravity
papers.abstract_en: We study single-field slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity (MAG). We consider the most general action up to operators linear in curvature and quadratic in the distortion, without propagating torsion and non-metricity. We first impose projective invariance and promote every coefficient to a function of the scalar field. After integrating out the non-dynamical distortion, the net contribution is a correction $k(φ)$ to the scalar kinetic term. We then consider the class of $ξ$-attractors for which the non-minimal couplings and the scalar potential are fixed by a single function $f(φ)$. It is well-known that in the metric formulation the strong-coupling regime is universally the Starobinsky attractor. In the Palatini framework, instead, this attractor is lost and the predictions become model-dependent. Here, we show that the MAG framework restores universality: in the strong coupling limit with finite ratios of the distortion couplings to $ξ$ we have an $α$-attractor, $n_s=1-2/N_*$ and $r=12α/N_*^2$, with $α=1+ζ/(6ξ)$. The ratio $ζ/ξ$ encodes the distortion contribution. Starobinsky and Palatini inflation are recovered as specific limits. Through a numerical parameter scan we show that almost all the healthy points lie on one of the two attractors : either Nieh-Yan-like inflation (studied in a previous work and extended here) or the new MAG $α$-attractor found here. Finally, we explicitly drop projective invariance and analyse the general MAG theory. The same large-field asymptotic structure survives. We conclude that no extra inflationary phenomenology is reached by the non-projectively invariant operators: the $α$-attractor is a general prediction of MAG.

papers.title_en: Probing the dynamics of extreme galaxies I. Dark matter content in ultra-diffuse galaxies
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the internal structure of two galaxies from the LEWIS sample: the ultra-diffuse galaxy UDG-1 and the extended dwarf LSB-6. Both show coherent stellar rotation combined with a non-negligible fraction of random motion, with no signs of ongoing disturbance. This is the first attempt to constrain the dynamics and dark matter physics of rotation-supported UDGs through integral-field stellar kinematics. We model the galaxies as stellar spheroids with typical dwarf-like thickness embedded in spherical dark matter halos, deriving two-dimensional velocity fields that we compare with the observations in a Bayesian framework. Besides cold dark matter, we test fuzzy, self-interacting, and non-minimally coupled dark matter. The data prefer a cuspy halo in UDG-1 and a cuspless one in LSB-6. All the alternative models remain viable, although current data cannot conclusively discriminate among them. For fuzzy dark matter we obtain mutually consistent boson masses, $m_α= 4.7^{+1.8}_{-1.1} \times 10^{-22}$ eV for UDG-1 and $m_α= 6.3^{+0.4}_{-0.4} \times 10^{-22}$ eV for LSB-6. For self-interacting dark matter, LSB-6 yields a robust constraint on the velocity-weighted cross section, $\langle σv\rangle/m = 14.3^{+2.0}_{-1.9}$ cm$^2$ km g$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. For non-minimally coupled dark matter we derive upper bounds on the coupling length, implying marginal deviations from $Λ$CDM. Regardless of the model, both galaxies exhibit a dark matter content comparable with halos of typical dwarf galaxies with similar stellar masses. Together with stellar population analyses and globular cluster information, these results support a scenario in which UDG-1 and LSB-6 originate from puffed-up dwarfs. This work is the first in a series exploiting kinematic data of extremely low-surface-brightness galaxies to test fundamental physics, from dark matter to modified theories of gravity.
papers.journal_ref: F. Bouchè et al., Probing the dynamics of extreme galaxies I. Dark matter content in ultra-diffuse galaxies, Astron. Astrophys. 715, A38 (2026)

papers.title_en: Can Magnetic Reconnection Accelerate Energetic Particles in the Heliosheath?
papers.abstract_en: The mechanism for accelerating energetic particles in the outer heliosphere is still under debate. The termination shock, turbulence, and magnetic reconnection have all been proposed as viable mechanisms. We investigate compression-driven particle acceleration during magnetic reconnection in the heliospheric current sheet using the MHD--SDE framework that incorporates energetic-particle feedback into the MHD evolution. For the heliosheath conditions considered here, we find that reconnection-driven acceleration is inefficient downstream of the termination shock, whereas reconnection near the heliopause can generate stronger compression and produce a power-law differential intensity spectrum $J(\varepsilon)\propto\varepsilon^{-5.4}$. However, even the hardest spectrum achieved during magnetic reconnection remains much steeper than the typical $J(\varepsilon)\propto\varepsilon^{-1.5}$ spectrum observed in the heliosheath. This indicates that magnetic reconnection alone is insufficient to explain the acceleration of energetic particles in the heliosheath.

papers.title_en: Circling in on correlation functions in $\mathcal{N}=2$ orbifold theories
papers.abstract_en: We review the harmonic superspace formalism for 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories and apply it to orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. These theories have a remarkably similar description to $\mathcal N=4$ SYM, but their planar supergraphs feature topological twist lines which generate phases when intersecting bifundamental hypermultiplet propagators. These cause twisted sector BPS correlators to depend on the coupling $g$. Twisted Coulomb-branch operators of length $L$ receive a leading perturbative contribution to their two-point function at order $\mathcal{O}(g^{2L})$ from a supergraph involving a wrapped hypermultiplet circle. After performing the complete $D$-algebra, we show that the supergraph reduces to the universal conformal period $W_L=\binom{2L}{L}ζ(2L-1)$. We extend this analysis to multiple nested hypermultiplet circles and show that they reproduce a series of higher-order terms in the exact localisation result. A subsequent evaluation of leading contributions to BPS three-point correlators again shows complete agreement with localisation results in extremal case and generates new perturbative data in the non-extremal case. The latter involves one untwisted BPS descendant, which contains physical hypermultiplet fields and can therefore connect directly to the twist-dependent hypermultiplet circle. This reduces the suppression in $g$, resulting in a contribution $4 g^{2(\ell+1)} W_{\ell+1}$ controlled by a bridge length $\ell$ rather than by an external operator length $L\geq\ell$. These examples demonstrate the feasibility of harmonic superspace calculations in orbifold theories and point to various future applications in the context of non-BPS correlators, integrability and marginal deformations.

papers.title_en: Twisted Correlators from Harmonic Superspace
papers.abstract_en: We establish a harmonic superspace formulation for $\mathcal N=2$ orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. We account for the orbifold projection by introducing topological defect lines to the planar supergraphs of $\mathcal N=4$ SYM. These twist lines are sourced by twisted sector operators, transparent to vector multiplets but generate orbifold phases when crossed by bifundamental hypermultiplet fields. This formalism establishes a refinement of the orbifold inheritance principle at supergraph level. As a direct application, we compute leading twist-dependent corrections to BPS two- and three-point functions, finding agreement with localisation results in extremal cases and generating new data for non-extremal correlators. We further map these corrections to finite-size effects in the twisted hexagon formalism. This opens a path towards an all-order integrability prescription of orbifold structure constants.

papers.title_en: Lorentz Violation and Vector Meson Dominance
papers.abstract_en: Vector meson dominance models describe the mixing of photons with vector mesons; the hadronic admixture frequently dominates the interactions of photons with nucleons. This mixing also makes it possible to test for new physics affecting the vector mesons using photon measurements. The possibilities for new physics to be contrained in this indirect fashion include potential Lorentz and CPT violations in the hadronic effective action. The characteristic scale of bounds on Lorentz violation coefficients in the $ρ^{0}$ meson sector is two orders of magnitude weaker than the corresponding photon bounds, three orders of magnitude weaker for $φ$ vector mesons, and four orders of magnitude weaker for $ω$ mesons.

papers.title_en: Probing Solar-Wind Structure During Crab Pulsar Conjunctions with Dispersion and Faraday Rotation
papers.abstract_en: Observations of the Crab pulsar (PSR B0531+21) during solar conjunction probe plasma structure in the inner solar wind through radio-propagation effects. We analyze dispersion measure (DM) and rotation measure (RM) measurements from the annual conjunctions of 2022-2026, obtained with the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME). The 2025 DM time series is distinguished from those of the other years by a secondary enhancement on 21 June, about one week after the main conjunction peak. In our scattering-corrected DM measurements, this feature, $Δ$DM $= (3.95 \pm 0.20) \times 10^{-3}$ pc cm$^{-3}$, is about 20 times the day-to-day DM scatter outside the conjunction window. The RM time series, measured by combining the single pulses of each observation and corrected for the ionospheric contribution, show conjunction excursions of up to $\sim 60$ rad m$^{-2}$ and changes of sign consistent with crossings of heliospheric magnetic-sector boundaries, but no counterpart to the secondary 2025 DM feature or to a similar post-conjunction DM tail in 2026. From the slope of the RM excess against the DM excess we estimate the electron-density-weighted line-of-sight magnetic field; for the sectors with significant slopes, $|\langle B_\parallel \rangle|$ is at least $\sim 0.2$ to $\sim 10$ mG near conjunction, largest in 2025.

papers.title_en: Unveiling the nonthermal environments of NGC 3411 and NGC 5903 through new MeerKAT observations
papers.abstract_en: Galaxy groups are key laboratories for investigating the interplay between active galactic nucleus (AGN) outbursts and the dynamical processes of the intra-group medium. We aim to characterize the morphology, spectral properties, and magnetic field structure of the diffuse nonthermal radio emission in two peculiar galaxy groups, NGC 3411 and NGC 5903, selected from an originally larger sample, in order to constrain its origin and its connection with the dynamics of the intra-group medium. We present new MeerKAT UHF- and L-band observations of the two groups, complemented by archival Chandra and XMM-Newton data already analyzed in previous works. In NGC 3411, we detect extended radio emission surrounding the central AGN over scales of ~70 kpc, and resolve previously undetected arc-shaped substructures on scales of ~20-30 kpc. This extended component exhibits a relatively uniform steep spectrum ($α$ ~ -1.7). We discuss possible scenarios for its origin, including mini-halos, aged AGN plasma, weak shocks, and the possibility of a radio galaxy observed along the line of sight. In NGC 5903, MeerKAT reveals a complex filamentary morphology, including a previously unknown ring-like structure surrounding the central AGN. Spectral-index mapping shows localized flattening ($α$ ~ -0.9) along the north arc, while polarization data reveal ordered magnetic fields and a patchy rotation measure distribution across the source. Together with the disturbed X-ray morphology, these results support a scenario in which fossil AGN plasma has been redistributed and locally reenergized by group-scale dynamical processes such as turbulence, shear, and weak compression. Our results demonstrate that galaxy groups can host a rich variety of nonthermal phenomena, whose properties can only be fully revealed through the combination of sensitive, high-resolution, and multifrequency radio observations.

papers.title_en: Majorana-like Josephson branch structure in one-dimensional transport of cold atoms
papers.abstract_en: We study phase-controlled transport through a one-dimensional channel of attractively interacting fermions connecting two three-dimensional BCS reservoirs. The competition between channel phase stiffness and pair tunnelling at the two contacts results in the emergence of two $4π$-periodic families of stationary states, characterised by symmetric or asymmetric phase drops at the boundaries. Advancing the reservoir phase difference by $2π$ exchanges these families so that the equilibrium energy remains $2π$ periodic, while the $4π$ periodicity might be attained in a diabatic regime. This structure admits a formal description in terms of two boundary Majorana operators, combining into a nonlocal fermion mode. Renormalization-group analysis shows that quantum fluctuations and phase slips are suppressed in the zero-temperature thermodynamic limit, preserving the branch crossings. The predicted branch exchange, metastable currents, and sweep-rate-dependent switching provide experimentally testable signatures of Majorana-like Josephson branch physics in a gapless interacting channel.

papers.title_en: Finite-volume effects on smeared spectral densities
papers.abstract_en: Using two distinct approaches, we derive a universal expression for the leading finite-volume effects of the smeared vector-vector spectral density (proportional to the smeared hadronic $R$-ratio) in a periodic cubic spatial volume of side length $L$. First, building on the results of previous work for finite-volume effects on Euclidean two-point functions, we show that the $L$ dependence is exponentially suppressed for a certain class of smearing kernels, and that the leading effects can be expressed universally in terms of the pion form factor. The same representation is then derived starting from the Lellouch-Lüscher-Meyer expression for the spectral decomposition of the correlator. The results may prove useful for controlling the $L \to \infty$ extrapolation of smeared spectral densities, in particular by defining a scaling regime in which the finite-volume effects are dominated by the leading terms in a large $L$ expansion and thus can be reliably estimated. To illustrate this point, we also present numerical estimates based on various kernels and models of particle interactions. Despite focusing on the vector channel, our derivation defines a general framework applicable to other cases as well.

papers.title_en: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
papers.abstract_en: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a low-temperature anisotropic phase accompanied by a Fermi surface reconstruction. Near the stripe-to-superconductor transition, we also observed an additional thermodynamic phase transition from metallic stripes to pinned insulating stripes. The stripe-to-superconductor transition further exhibits an intriguing self-similarity that highlights the intimate relationship between the two orders. Our results pave the path for studying intertwined orders in moiré materials.

papers.title_en: Form Factors in AdS from the Worldsheet
papers.abstract_en: We study AdS form factors describing closed strings scattering off D-branes. Assuming that these form factors admit worldsheet integral representations in terms of multiple polylogarithms, we determine their leading curvature corrections around the flat-space limit by matching their pole structure to CFT data. We focus on two examples of defects in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM: a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS 't Hooft loop, dual to a D1 brane, and a pair of giant gravitons, dual to a D3 brane. For the 't Hooft loop, the worldsheet bootstrap completely fixes the form factor, and the result passes nontrivial checks from supersymmetric localization. For the giant gravitons, the bootstrap initially leaves five free coefficients, one of which can be fixed using localization. Remarkably, imposing instead that no new operators appear in the defect channel at this order fixes all five coefficients and reproduces the localization constraint. Under this additional assumption, we therefore obtain a unique D3-brane form factor, with supersymmetric localization providing an independent check.

papers.title_en: Born-Infeld black holes in bumblebee gravity
papers.abstract_en: We construct exact static and spherically symmetric charged solutions in bumblebee gravity minimally coupled to Born--Infeld electrodynamics, taking into account a spacelike vector norm and a vanishing cosmological constant. An independently varied Lagrange multiplier enforces the norm constraint and acquires a radial profile determined by the transverse electromagnetic pressure. The solutions include purely radial configurations and configurations with constant or varying temporal amplitudes. At $ξ=κ/2$, the varying temporal amplitude introduces an independent bumblebee field strength while preserving the metric of the constant temporal configuration. Moreover, the electric field remains bounded, and the temporal configurations admit smooth extensions across a simple future horizon under explicit regularity conditions. We derive the photon sphere and shadow radii for both metric and nonlinear electromagnetic propagation. The leading nonlinear corrections enlarge the shadow at fixed geometric charge, whereas the temporal amplitude enters through the charged lapse. Comparisons with observations of Sgr~A$^*$ and M87$^*$ provide conditional bounds on the charge and nonlinear scale. In addition, the adopted planetary perihelion allowances yield an illustrative sensitivity of $|ξ|(b^2+u_0^2)\lesssim2.6\times10^{-12}$ for a neutral solar exterior.

papers.title_en: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract_en: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.

papers.title_en: Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting electronics
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top $α$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rmα$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $μ$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.

papers.title_en: Quantum field theory treatment of the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos with diagonal magnetic moments
papers.abstract_en: We apply the quantum field theory (QFT) approach to describe the spin-flavor precession of Dirac neutrinos. The magnetic moments matrix of these neutrinos is taken to be diagonal in the mass basis. Neutrino mass eigenstates are considered to be virtual particles in the QFT approach. The neutrino contribution to the matrix element of the overall process, which includes the emission, the propagation and the detection of neutrinos, is contained in the propagators of massive neutrinos. Using the recently derived propagator of a massive neutrino, which exactly accounts for the magnetic moment interaction, we derive the transition probability of the process $ν_{e\mathrm{L}}\toν_{μ\mathrm{L}}$ under the influence of a magnetic field. The result is compared with the prediction of the standard quantum mechanical (QM) approach. We briefly discuss the possibility to derive the QFT corrections to the QM expressions.

papers.title_en: APOLLO-Timing: Annealed Phase - Orbit Lattice Linking across Observations for Binary Pulsar Timing
papers.abstract_en: Sparse observations of binary pulsars can leave the orbit and the pulse count across observing gaps uncertain. We present APOLLO-Timing, a Bayesian phase-orbit lattice method that fits timing parameters together with integer pulse offsets between observing sessions. PINT checks the candidate connections at fixed pulse numbers. For PSR J1912-1215, a preliminary Keplerian fit to variations in the apparent spin period and its derivative did not phase-connect 96 times of arrival (TOAs) spanning 1438.07 days in 23 sessions. Starting from its position, spin frequency F0, and first time derivative F1 estimated in that fit, with dispersion measure fixed, APOLLO-Timing recovers the orbit and a unique best-supported phase-connected solution without supplied orbital parameters. A repeat full-data blind search recovers the same pulse counts in 914.0 s, including the final fit. Setting the initial F1 to zero in the 17, 18, and 19 session subsets also recovers the reference path. The solution gives Pb = 17.526 days, x = 23.448 light-seconds, e = 2.65e-5, chi-square = 188.01, and a weighted rms residual of 5.08 microseconds. For a pulsar mass of 1.4 solar masses and inclination of 60 degrees, the inferred companion mass is 0.67 solar masses, favoring a CO/ONeMg white dwarf.

papers.title_en: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract_en: We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^\natural$ and formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own.

papers.title_en: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
papers.abstract_en: Blackbody radiation (BBR) poses a central challenge for quantum science with Rydberg atoms. By driving transitions to nearby opposite-parity states, BBR shortens Rydberg lifetimes and has long been suspected to trigger "avalanche" events known to cause correlated atom loss. Here, we suppress avalanche decay and establish BBR as its dominant trigger using a Rydberg atom array that operates either cryogenically or at room temperature. A $45~\text{K}$ radiation shield reduces ambient BBR, extending Rydberg $nS$ lifetimes for $n$ ranging from 50 to 75. BBR-induced decay rates are suppressed by 30%-50%, corresponding to an effective blackbody temperature $T_{\rm eff}\approx190~\text{K}$. This enables controlled comparisons of Rydberg-dressed atom arrays operating in different BBR environments. Arrays of up to 70 atoms demonstrate cryogenically suppressed avalanche rates, tracking the suppression in BBR-induced decay, for both $n=50$ and $n=60$ dressing. A parameter-free rate model agrees with the measured avalanche rates after accounting for frequency-dependent cryogenic shielding, photoionization-triggered avalanches, laser phase noise, BBR decay channels, and Rydberg interaction effects. We demonstrate a quantitative description of avalanche decay and show that improved BBR shielding should further suppress correlated loss to the $T_\text{eff}=45~\text{K}$ achievable in the current apparatus. Our results establish a route to mitigating correlated errors that otherwise impede fault-tolerant operation in neutral-atom quantum processors.

papers.title_en: MACE: Multigroup-Multiangle Integrated Thermal Compton Scattering Kernel
papers.abstract_en: We present a comprehensive set of accurate Compton-scattering tables for use in multigroup, multiangle radiation-transport calculations. The tables contain the exact thermal Compton kernel integrated over incident-energy groups, scattered-energy groups, and angular bins. To generate them, we develop a deterministic integration method in which the pointwise kernel is evaluated with a robust numerical treatment that remains accurate across challenging regions of parameter space. The multidimensional integrals are computed using nested quadratures whose panels adapt to the Compton recoil ridge, its thermal broadening, and the nearly elastic forward-scattering boundary layer. We validate the tabulated results against published kernel profiles, angular and energy moments, mean free paths, multigroup redistribution data, and an independent Monte Carlo estimator. The resulting tables provide the radiation-transport community with accurate, reproducible, and readily usable Compton redistribution matrices and angular moments.

papers.title_en: IceCube data for astrophysical neutrinos exhibit q-statistical behavior
papers.abstract_en: Relevant IceCube recent data for astrophysical neutrinos are analyzed. Similarly to cosmic rays and proton-proton LHC collisions, the corresponding spectra are satisfactorily described, for the entire interval of measured energies, through $q$-Gaussians. This fact reinforces the already available evidence that nonadditive entropies (either of the $S_q$ class or of the $S_δ$ one, or even alternative ones) appear to play a crucial role in systems such as black holes and related cosmological phenomena (e.g., dark energy). The IceCube data yield high values for the momenta-distribution nonadditive index ($q \simeq 1.6$, hence $q_{energy} \simeq 1.3$), to be compared with the cosmic rays values ($q_{energy} \simeq 1.2$) and the LHC values ($q_{energy} \simeq 1.1$). This fact neatly indicates very-long-ranged space-time correlations. The detailed associated physical mechanisms remain, at the present stage, as an instigating open issue.

papers.title_en: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
papers.abstract_en: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

papers.title_en: IceCube Real-time Searches for High-energy Neutrinos Coincident with LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Alerts in O4a
papers.abstract_en: Gravitational-wave events from mergers of compact objects are a predicted source of high-energy neutrinos. Using data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, we search for neutrinos coincident with 85 significant and 945 low-significance gravitational-wave candidate events from compact binary coalescences published in real-time by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration during the first part of its fourth observing run (O4a) and its preceding engineering run, within a time window of $\pm500$ seconds from the merger time. We report improvements to the online pipelines, including automatic sending of notices, which improved the median IceCube real-time response compared to the previous observing run by a factor of 2.7 times faster. In addition, we search for long-duration neutrino emission from three candidate events: two neutron star-black hole mergers and one low-significance gravitational-wave event with a possible subthreshold gamma-ray counterpart. We use two methods, both of which have been previously used to search for neutrinos from gravitational-wave transients: an unbinned maximum likelihood analysis on significant alerts and a Bayesian analysis accounting for astrophysical priors on all alerts. We find no statistically significant emission from any individual gravitational-wave event analyzed. In the unbinned maximum likelihood search, the lowest $p$-value event is S231029y, with $p=0.0079$ ($0.752$ post-trials). In the Bayesian search, the lowest $p$-value for significant events is S230904n, with $p=0.0076$ ($0.9996$ post-trials), and for low-significance events is S231025a, with $p=0.0011$ ($0.678$ post-trials), with an overall population $p$-value of $0.55$. We accordingly set upper limits for each event on the time-integrated flux and energy emitted in neutrinos, assuming isotropic emission.

papers.title_en: Dynamically Reentrant Skyrmion Phase in Oscillating Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract_en: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

papers.title_en: $d$-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$
papers.abstract_en: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state is energetically favored, while extended $s$-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below $T_c$, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows $1/T_1T\propto T^2$, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust $d$-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO$_{2}$, while trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{8}$ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between $d$-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

papers.title_en: Dipolar boson stars as static two-body systems: an effective-one-body description
papers.abstract_en: Dipolar boson stars consist of two scalar-field lumps held in static equilibrium by the balance between gravitational attraction and scalar repulsion. The repulsion stems from a $π$ phase difference between the harmonically varying complex scalar field sourcing each lump. We construct sequences of these configurations numerically and describe them analytically as bound states of two boson stars within the effective-one-body (EOB) formalism. We map the EOB potential previously derived for the scattering of two boson stars onto an energy-dependent Schwarzschild-like radial potential. We find that the EOB-based analytical prediction for the binding energy of the system agrees remarkably well with the numerical values. The analytical prediction for the critical gravitational coupling beyond which no static equilibrium exists is also consistent with the numerical results.

papers.title_en: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
papers.abstract_en: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.

papers.title_en: Probing black bounce spacetime through mass accretion rate
papers.abstract_en: We study steady, spherically symmetric accretion of a collisionless kinetic gas onto a compact object described by the Simpson--Visser (SV) metric, a one-parameter regularization of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Using the standard relativistic Vlasov formalism, we adopt boundary conditions at a finite injection radius $R$ and compute the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$ for Vlasov gas with both monoenergetic and Maxwell--Jüttner distribution functions. Throughout the computation, we also take into account the influence of particle's angular momentum. We carefully investigate the influence of the black bounce parameter on the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$. By expanding accretion rate in terms of bounce parameter $a$, we found that the leading-order correction appears at quadratic order in $a$. This work extends the Vlasov accretion framework to a broader class of spherically symmetric spacetimes and quantifies the impact of the geometric modification on the accretion flow. In particular, since the shadows of the SV and Schwarzschild black holes are degenerate, comparing their mass accretion rates may offer a complementary probe for distinguishing these geometries in future astrophysical observations.

papers.title_en: Field evolution of the multi-$k$ magnetic states in NdB$_4$ revealed by neutron diffraction
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the magnetic states of the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice magnet NdB$_4$ using single-crystal neutron diffraction. We focus on magnetic fields applied along the tetragonal $c$ axis, which stabilise the fractional 1/5~magnetisation plateau. In the low-temperature phase below 4.9 K, the transition into the plateau state at approximately 12 kOe is marked by a change in the propagation vectors from $(1/5,0,-2/5)$ and its double $(2/5,0,1/5)$ to $(0,0,1/5)$ and $(0,0,2/5)$. At the transition from the plateau to a nominally `field-polarised' state near 33 kOe, all magnetic reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, whereas reflections corresponding to the $\mathbf{k}=0$ component persist throughout the entire field range. We conclude that that the in-plane components survive even in the high-field phase and that the polarisation is, in fact, incomplete. The observed field dependence provides direct support for a description of NdB$_4$ in terms of two coupled magnetic instabilities: all-in-all-out order of the in-plane moments and a spin-density wave of the out-of-plane components.

papers.title_en: Quasinormal modes of charged de Sitter black holes and strong cosmic censorship in conformal Killing gravity
papers.abstract_en: The strong cosmic censorship conjecture argues that the future evolution of the spacetime should be predictable from the initial data. However, within the framework of general relativity, some counterexamples to the conjecture have been found, especially for de Sitter spacetime. Spurred by challenges to the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, we extend such investigations to conformal Killing gravity, a promising candidate beyond Einstein's theory. Considering neutral massless scalar perturbations for charged de Sitter black hole, we not only shed light on the quasinormal mode spectrum, but also clarify whether the modifications from conformal Killing gravity and nonlinear electrodynamics can rescue the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, and further investigate how characteristic parameters affect its validity. As the first instance for investigating the conjecture in the framework of conformal Killing gravity, this paper reports some unexpected findings.

papers.title_en: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
papers.abstract_en: We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and exhibit suitable gauge-invariant probes on which the induced transformations act nontrivially.

papers.title_en: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
papers.abstract_en: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.

papers.title_en: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
papers.abstract_en: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.

papers.title_en: Relativistic Elasticity II
papers.abstract_en: This paper is based on a series of talks given at the ESI program on 'Mathematical Perspectives of Gravitation Beyond the Vacuum Regime' in February 2022. It is meant to be an introduction to the field of relativistic elasticity for readers with a good base in the mathematics of General Relativity with no necessary previous of knowledge of elasticity either in the classical or relativistic domain. Despite its introductory purpose, the present work has new material, in particular related to the formal structure of the theory.

papers.title_en: Precision Solar System Dynamics for Ultralight Dark Matter Search
papers.abstract_en: Ultralight dark matter exhibits an order-one density fluctuation at the scale of its wavelength. This density fluctuation exists across the entire dark matter halo and interacts with stars and planets, perturbing their motion via gravitational interactions. We investigate the possibility of using precision solar system dynamics to search for ultralight dark matter. We examine this possibility with interplanetary radio range measurements. We show that the precision of current range measurements can probe ultralight dark matter at masses around $10^{-15}\,$eV, had its density in the solar system been $10^5$ larger than the so-called local dark matter density. This limit complements other constraints, such as the one from analyses of pulsar timing observations.

papers.title_en: QUIJOTE scientific results -- XVIII. New constraints on the polarization of the Anomalous Microwave Emission in bright Galactic regions: $ρ$\,Ophiuchi, Perseus and W43
