We present a tensor-network method that chooses no subsystems and whose memory and run time per solve are set by the number of modes and two truncations, the Fock cutoff of each normal mode and the bond dimension of a matrix product state (MPS), not by the Hilbert-space dimension. From the capacitance matrix, the inverse-inductance matrix and the junction list alone, the linear circuit is diagonalized into normal modes. Each junction cosine is then a sum of two products of single-mode operators, so the complete lumped-element Hamiltonian is a matrix product operator (MPO) of small bond dimension with one site per mode, solved by the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). The normal modes make the method generic, and the tensor network makes it affordable. For two fluxonia joined by a tunable coupler, the method agrees with exact diagonalization of the same truncated space to within 1 MHz. Our circuit of three fluxonia joined by two couplers has 11 normal modes and a truncated space of $10^9$ states, out of reach of exact diagonalization in dense or sparse storage. At a bond dimension of 32, its lowest eight levels are converged to within 1 MHz in both truncations, and each state is stored in a small fraction of the numbers a dense vector needs. One solve at that bond dimension takes 81 min and 1.3 GB of memory on one CPU node.

papers.title_en: Indirect probes of heavy neutral leptons through the dipole portal at FCC-ee
papers.abstract_en: We study indirect probes of the gauge-invariant dipole portal of Majorana heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at FCC-ee. Virtual HNLs modify electroweak gauge-boson propagation and lepton couplings through loops with two dipole interactions. We calculate the resulting finite matching corrections and their effects on $Z$-pole observables. For real, flavour-aligned couplings, the local response is specified by four combinations of coupling shifts. Independent local ultraviolet interactions can reproduce all four, making the dipole interpretation dependent on assumptions about those interactions. With improved Standard Model predictions, FCC-ee can probe equal, same-sign hypercharge and weak dipole coefficients as small as $0.14\,\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$ at an HNL mass of 1 TeV. This projection assumes dipole dominance, with independent ultraviolet coefficients set to zero at twice the HNL mass. We quantify how additional ultraviolet contributions can weaken or strengthen the sensitivity. At 1 TeV, the projected reach is competitive with HL-LHC same-sign dilepton searches for Majorana HNLs, while larger masses allow smaller dipole coefficients to be probed within the effective theory's domain of validity. Radiative Higgs decays offer a modest further improvement. The FeynRules, FeynArts and UFO models used in this analysis are publicly available at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667622}{doi:10.5281/zenodo.23667622}.

papers.title_en: Classical training of conditional instantaneous quantum polynomial-time Born machines
papers.abstract_en: Instantaneous quantum polynomial-time (IQP) Born machines are attractive quantum generative models, as certain IQP circuit families are conjectured to be hard to sample, yet they can be trained classically. Previously proposed conditional IQP Born machines make the parameters of the diagonal layer condition dependent. We introduce conditional IQP Born machines, in which the condition is encoded in the input state and a single IQP unitary is shared across conditions. Efficient sampling and amplitude-ratio evaluation for the reference state entering the diagonal layer suffice to obtain unbiased classical estimates of a conditional maximum mean discrepancy objective and its gradients. We show that input conditioning can represent conditional families that no diagonally conditioned IQP model with the same number of qubits can reproduce. For the sixteen-qubit Curie-Weiss spin model, a single conditional model captures the magnetization transition at held-out temperatures. Its mean total variation distance is six times lower than that of diagonal conditioning under the same protocol and comparable to that of classical generative models with up to seven times as many parameters. We also train conditional models classically with up to 2048 qubits, which reproduce the mean squared magnetization of the target away from the crossover. These results extend classically trained IQP Born machines to conditional generation.

papers.title_en: The most entangled states of four and seven qubits
papers.abstract_en: Pure states of four and seven qubits cannot be maximally entangled across every balanced bipartition; we determine how entangled they can be on average. For four qubits we prove the conjecture of Higuchi and Sudbery: the mean von Neumann entropy of the three $2|2$ cuts is at most $1+\tfrac12\log_2 3$ bits, with equality exactly on the local-unitary orbits of their state $M_4$ and its complex conjugate. For seven qubits the mean purity of the 35 balanced $3|4$ cuts is at least $121/917$ and their mean entropy is at most $2.965356029\ldots$ bits, each with a unique optimiser up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. The two optimisers are distinct members of one icosahedral family, so minimum purity and maximum entropy select different states. The proofs bound moments of the marginal spectra by positive identities on several copies of the state, some of them spin flipped, and bound the entropy by a polynomial in those moments. The four-qubit maximum has an analytic proof; the seven-qubit proofs, and some of the four-qubit refinements below, are computer-assisted, with exact arithmetic and rigorous error bounds. We also prove the Gour--Wallach conjecture for Rényi entropies of all orders, with the maximiser changing from $M_4$ to cluster states at $q_*\approx1.588$, and obtain sharp Tsallis bounds, mixed-state bounds and quantitative stability.

papers.title_en: Quantum theory of damping: A new approach to temporal evolution of density operator without the rotating wave approximation
papers.abstract_en: The Lindblad master equation is the standard framework for describing dissipative dynamics of the open quantum system context. Its conventional derivation, however, relies on the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), which neglects the counter rotating terms in the system-reservoir interaction. Here, we derive a generalized Lindblad master equation beyond the RWA within the density operator formalism, retaining the full systemreservoir coupling. We consider two prototypical open quantum systems, a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized field, each interacting with thermal or squeezed reservoirs described by the Wigner-Weisskopf theory. The resulting master equations are applied to the evolution of representative physical observables and compared with the conventional RWA based formulation. We show that counter-rotating terms produce significant modifications to the dissipative dynamics and therefore cannot, in general, be neglected. For a thermal reservoir, increasing the mean thermal photon number, nth, enhances the decay of hσ^yi beyond the RWA but suppresses it within the RWA. Likewise, the evolution of hσ^zi exhibits opposite damping behavior with increasing Γt and squeezing parameter r. These findings demonstrate the importance of including counter rotating terms for an accurate description of open quantum systems.

papers.title_en: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
papers.abstract_en: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

papers.title_en: Trinetra.Q: Statistical and Behavioral Detection of Attacks on the Quantum-Error-Correction Layer and Classical Control Stack of Quantum Computing Systems
papers.abstract_en: Most quantum-computer security work targets physical-layer attacks on qubits, while two surfaces remain inadequately defended: the quantum-error-correction (QEC) syndrome-and-decoder pipeline, and the classical control and software stack that runs it. Tampering on these surfaces can corrupt a computation while the physical error rate appears normal, and can stay within a single-circuit integrity tolerance. We present Trinetra.Q, a detection layer of cooperating detectors, each monitoring a statistical or behavioral property of quantum-domain data against an envelope calibrated from honest operation, and raising an indication only on a statistically significant deviation. The detectors cover (A) QEC integrity over per-stabilizer firing rates, syndrome defect-count, and repeated-syndrome rate; (B) decoder confidence over the margin between minimum-weight error explanations in distinct logical classes; (C) behavioral output divergence, flagging crosstalk-class and novel attacks by their effect on a victim's output relative to a matched control; (D) control-stack tampering via known-answer canary circuits, built to be indistinguishable to a resident implant, with a cross-job consistency statistic; and (E) compilation/execution integrity. Each gates on significance, so honest operation raises no alarm. We evaluate in faithful simulation and on three production IBM Heron processors, and bound the physical attack surface with a systematic negative map: most physical-layer attacks return statistically null, the exception an implemented, measured within-job feed-forward covert-channel primitive. Every detector is also evaluated against an adaptive attacker with full knowledge of it. To our knowledge this is the first unified statistical-and-behavioral detection layer for the QEC layer and classical control stack of a quantum computing system, demonstrated on production hardware.

papers.title_en: Multipartite entanglement swapping with homodyne and single photon detection
papers.abstract_en: Establishing multipartite entanglement across lossy optical networks remains a central challenge for distributed quantum information processing. Here, we consider a non-Gaussian continuous-variable entanglement-swapping protocol combining a symmetric discrete Fourier transform (DFT) interferometer with photon-number-resolving detection. In the ideal limit, single-photon heralding generates a $W_N$-class state across remote modes, with Fourier symmetry rendering all single-click outcomes equivalent up to local phase corrections. We find that conditional pairwise entanglement can exceed that of conventional Gaussian homodyne swapping in weak-to-moderate squeezing and lossy regimes, remaining nonzero beyond the channel-loss thresholds at which Gaussian pairwise entanglement vanishes. These results demonstrate that combining non-Gaussian measurements with symmetric interferometric mixing can improve both the resilience and operational efficiency of multipartite entanglement distribution in lossy quantum networks.

papers.title_en: Efficient training of a 128-modes 3D continuously coupled photonic chip via limited quantum resources
papers.abstract_en: Integrated photonics provides a promising route towards the development of large-scale, stable and low-loss quantum hardware. Existing implementations of universal quantum photonic chips generally rely on architectures consisting of localised interactions between the modes that can be programmed with known algorithms to implement specific operations. Recent advances have shown that interferometers based on 3D continuously coupled waveguide arrays may allow to significantly scale up the number of modes with reduced overhead. However, for this class of devices, optimal strategies to set the controllable parameters and obtain the desired transformation have not been demonstrated generally. In this work, we report the use of a machine learning algorithm driven by quantum data to program the operation of a reconfigurable three-dimensional continuously coupled photonic device comprising 128 modes. We show experimentally the capability of reaching a target unitary matrix, among those achievable by the device, through a limited number of one- and two-photon measurements. Our results demonstrate that this approach results to be effective in the presence of noise and with a limited amount of resources, also allowing to partially compensate imperfections in the experimental setup. This method can thus represent a viable route towards programming large scale integrated photonic devices, unlocking the possibility of controlling photonic systems for which an analytical decomposition is not trivial.

papers.title_en: Higher-order quantum information inequalities and error-correction of non-Markovian noise
papers.abstract_en: Defining entropy of a quantum channel has become a challenge with potential candidates recently reported in literature. In this Article, it is taken under consideration the entropy of a quantum channel defined as the quantum entropy of its associated Choi state. The consequences presented here of such approach is two-fold. First, the limitations on the information-processing of quantum channels are assessed, leading to the \emph{higher-order quantum information inequalities}. Those are then considered as useful witnesses of non-Markovian effects beyond a given number of quantum side-channels in a quantum process. Importantly, the presentation is given with the application of the methods for the study of examples. Second, such approach provides a characterization on the condition for the recovery of quantum channel preparations under non-Markovian noise. Such result is a straightforward extension of standard error-correction conditions which gives further meaning to the higher-order information measures defined here.

papers.title_en: Quantum resource trade-offs of mixed sparse single and double factorization for qubitization-based phase estimation
papers.abstract_en: We study a mixed block encoding of quantum-chemistry Hamiltonians for quantum phase estimation (QPE) on fault-tolerant quantum computers. Following a Cholesky decomposition of the electron repulsion integral tensor, we assign each Cholesky tensor to either a double-factorization (DF) branch or a sparse-single-factorization (SPSF) branch. This freedom permits a trade-off between reducing the block-encoding normalization factor $λ$ with DF and reducing the coefficient data loaded through quantum read-only memory (QROM) with SPSF. Resource estimates across molecular benchmarks show, however, that the mixed circuit does not generally reduce the Toffoli count relative to the less expensive pure circuit. The main obstacles are the overhead of loading substantial data through separate branch-specific QROMs and the limited benefit of mixing when the pure DF and SPSF circuits have dissimilar costs. Modest savings occur only in restricted parameter regimes, most clearly when logical-qubit requirements are included in the cost metric. These results identify the circuit-level conditions that a useful mixed block encoding must satisfy.

papers.title_en: A Study of Fluctuation Growths of Observables in Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract_en: The rate at which quantum fluctuations of observables can change provides a useful characterization of the dynamical behavior of quantum systems. For closed quantum systems undergoing unitary evolution, previous work has established a general upper bound on the growth rate of the uncertainty of an observable in terms of the standard deviation of its dynamical velocity. This result is closely related to quantum acceleration limits and provides a compact constraint on fluctuation growth. In this work, we will briefly review the closed system results and extend this perspective to open quantum systems, where the state evolves nonunitarily as a consequence of interactions with an environment. The central result is an upper bound on the rate of growth of the uncertainty of an observable that remains valid for general density-matrix dynamics. We develop two complementary derivations. The first introduces a Hermitian pseudo-Hamiltonian describing the local unitary evolution of the eigenvectors of the density matrix. The second, and more general, derivation proceeds directly from the density-matrix derivative and therefore does not require knowledge of the generator of the dynamics. Both approaches lead to the same fluctuation-growth bound. An important practical advantage is that the bound can be evaluated from the observable, the state, and its time derivative without requiring reconstruction of the complete dynamical generator.

papers.title_en: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
papers.abstract_en: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

papers.title_en: Charmonium production at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron and Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research
papers.abstract_en: In this study we apply the Remler formalism to charmonium production at Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and GSI/Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (FAIR) energies in order to investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions within the parton-hadron-string dynamics. As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> collisions and then applied to <math><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which <math><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>ψ</mi></mrow></math> dissociates near <math><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></math>. Finally, the same formalism is applied to the low CERN/SPS energy and GSI/FAIR energies, where we estimate charmonium production.

papers.title_en: Novel qubits in hybrid semiconductor–superconductor nanostructures
papers.abstract_en: In recent years, hybrid semiconductor–superconductor qubits have emerged as a compelling alternative to more traditional qubit platforms, owing to their unique combination of material properties and device-level tunability. A key feature of these systems is their gate-tunable Josephson coupling, which enables the realization of superconducting qubit architectures with full electric field control and which offers a promising route toward scalable and low-crosstalk quantum processors. One of the central motivations behind this approach is the possibility of unifying the advantages of superconducting and spin-based qubits. This approach to creating hybrid qubits can be achieved, for example, by encoding quantum information in the spin degree of freedom of a quasiparticle occupying an Andreev bound state, thereby combining long coherence times with fast and flexible control. Recent progress has been further accelerated by the bottom-up engineering of Andreev bound states into coupled quantum dot arrays, leading to the realization of novel device architectures such as minimal Kitaev chains hosting (poor man’s) Majorana states, precursors of topologically protected Majorana zero modes, and, very recently, to the first coherent control of a Majorana parity qubit. In parallel, alternative strategies have focused on the design of Hamiltonian-protected hybrid qubits, including Cooper pair parity qubits and fluxon parity qubits, which aim to enhance robustness against local noise and decoherence. These approaches leverage the interplay between superconducting phase dynamics and the discrete charge or flux degrees of freedom in hybrid junctions. In this article, we review recent theoretical and experimental advances in the development of semiconductor–superconductor hybrid qubits. We provide a comprehensive overview of the underlying physical mechanisms, device implementations, and emerging architectures, with particular emphasis on their potential to enable (topologically) protected quantum information processing. While many of these qubit designs remain at the proof-of-concept stage, the rapid pace of progress suggests that practical demonstrations may be within reach in the near future.

papers.title_en: Gauge-invariant fermion
papers.abstract_en: We show that in quantum electrodynamics the Green’s functions of the Dirac-dressed fermion coincide, for any value of the gauge parameter in the <math display="inline"><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ξ</mi></msub></math> gauge and to all orders in perturbation theory, with those of the undressed fermion in the Landau gauge. The dressed fermion couples only to the transverse photon, and the gauge parameter is confined to a decoupled sector. The dressed vertex then obeys a homogeneous Ward identity, and the dressed field is renormalized multiplicatively with no new counterterm. A partially dressed family realizes the Landau-Khalatnikov-Fradkin relation exactly, and dressings with other kernels reproduce other gauges. Every dressing yields the same pole mass, and assigning the off-shell differences between dressings to the vertex defines a common gauge-invariant mass function.

papers.title_en: Tidal gap: Causality bound on exotic compact objects
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we highlight the existence of a lower limit on the tidal deformability parameter <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></math> for static, isotropic compact objects. Additionally, by considering the corresponding upper bound on compactness, we identify the region within the compactness–tidal-deformability parameter space where physically motivated exotic compact objects could potentially reside. Our analysis reveals the presence of a “tidal gap” between black holes, characterized by vanishing tidal deformability, and horizonless compact objects. Prompted by this finding, we investigate the possibility that a population of maximally compact exotic objects described by a linear equation of state may simultaneously inhabit the lower-mass gap and the subsolar region, thus qualifying as (primordial) black hole mimickers while distinguishing themselves from the latter through their nonzero tidal deformability. We also provide an illustrative estimate of the prospects for probing their tidal response with present and future gravitational-wave detectors. Finally, considering solitonic boson stars as explicit field-theoretical exotic compact objects whose bulk structure approximately reproduces the linear equation of state, we show that values of <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></math> below the isotropic limit can be reached without violating relativistic causality. This result reflects the relaxation of the isotropic perfect-fluid and sharp-surface assumptions: the dominant energy condition remains satisfied, whereas the strong energy condition is locally violated near the effective surface.

papers.title_en: Subleading corrections to F-terms in the Large Volume Scenario
Axion-Like Particles
Analysis of the harmonic flow of geometric structures
Searches for dark photon via portal matter decay at the Large Hadron Collider
Time evolution of the <math><mi>α</mi></math>-decay process in intense laser fields
papers.abstract_en: Recently, influence of strong fields on nuclear decay processes is progressively becoming a topic of great interest plus the existence of some ambiguities. In this study, an approximate calculation of the Schrödinger equation with reduced <math><mi>r</mi></math> dependence is employed instead of the classical Coulomb wave-function program to provide a description of decay width and decay energy in quasistatic (adiabatic) laser fields. More importantly, going beyond the quasistatic approximation, the strict time evolution of the wave function and the periodic modulation of the decay energy are investigated by solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation with the split operator method, which captures the dynamical behavior of the <math><mi>α</mi></math> cluster during the decay process. First, our results corroborate earlier reports that the decay width is modified only negligibly by strong laser fields. Likewise, the shift in decay energy is found to be extremely small, which validates the rationality of using fixed experimental decay energies in earlier studies. This modification effect will exist more obviously in a nucleus with the higher proton-neutron asymmetry, the lower decay energy, and the octupole deformation. Second, our results demonstrate that strong fields can indeed produce a periodic modulation of decay energy, with a cycle mean shift on the order of <math><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="4pt"/><mi>eV</mi></mrow></math> at an intensity of <math><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>24</mn></msup><mspace width="4pt"/><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>.

papers.title_en: Dynamical and stable spin squeezing via magnon Kerr nonlinearity in a hybrid solid-state system
papers.abstract_en: Spin squeezing is a genuine multipartite entanglement resource enabling quantum-enhanced metrology beyond classical limits. Based on a hybrid solid-state system of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and magnons, we propose a scheme for generating spin squeezing via Kerr nonlinearity. In the large-detuning regime, by tuning the strength of the magnon parametric amplification (MPA) enabled by Kerr effect, the magnon-mediated spin-spin interactions can be controlled, thereby allowing flexible switching among one-axis twisting (OAT), two-axis twisting (TAT), and unconventional two-axis twisting (UTAT). Remarkably, in the presence of realistic dissipation and finite-size effects, an optimized UTAT interaction exhibits enhanced spin squeezing and quantum-enhanced sensing performance compared with the corresponding OAT and TAT cases. Furthermore, in the resonant and strongly dissipative regime, the MPA-induced TAT interaction and squeezed magnon reservoir jointly enable steady-state spin squeezing of the NV ensemble. Our results establish a unified and flexible scheme for generating both dynamical and steady-state spin squeezing, with potential applications in quantum-enhanced precision measurements.

papers.title_en: Nonreciprocal frequency conversion of single photons in a one-dimensional coupled-resonator waveguide
papers.abstract_en: We design an atom-waveguide system to achieve nonreciprocal frequency conversion. Single-photon frequency conversion is achieved through inelastic scattering mediated by the V-type giant atom with one transition coupled to a one-dimensional coupled-resonator waveguide (CRW) and the other transition coherently driven by a classical field. To quantitatively characterize the frequency-conversion efficiency, we define scattering flows by incorporating the corresponding group velocities. The reciprocity and nonreciprocity of the system can be characterized by the conversion-flow contrast. It is found that the single-photon frequency-conversion flow is closely related to the size of the giant atom and the phase difference between the coupling strengths at the two atom-CRW coupling sites. Under reciprocal conditions, the maximum conversion flow is strictly bounded by <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, regardless of how the giant atom size and the phase difference are tuned. When reciprocity is broken, tuning the coupling phase at a fixed giant atom size significantly enhances the maximum conversion flow, which can even reach unity. Meanwhile, the conversion-flow contrast reaches its extremal values, corresponding to perfect single-photon nonreciprocity.

papers.title_en: State Synthesis with an NP oracle
papers.abstract_en: In this note, I describe a quantum algorithm that prepares an arbitrary state $|ψ\rangle$ to inverse exponential precision in polynomial time by making queries to an $\mathsf{NP}$ oracle, assuming one can directly query entries of the state vector corresponding to $|ψ\rangle$. The previous best upper bound on the complexity class required by an oracle for this task was $\mathsf{PP}$. I provide evidence that $\mathsf{NP}$ is the best possible upper bound by showing that any quantum algorithm using a $\mathsf{P}$ oracle, or even a $\mathsf{P/poly}$ oracle, requires exponentially many queries. I also discuss some implications of this result for the $\mathsf{QMA}$ search-to-decision problem and unitary synthesis.

papers.title_en: MBUndo: Sound, Automatic, and Efficient Measurement-Based Uncomputation for Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract_en: Quantum programs that use temporary values, known as \emph{ancilla} qubits, must explicitly \emph{uncompute} each ancilla back to zero to ensure that the program produces correct outputs. Conventional uncomputation uses unitary quantum gates, whereas leading quantum algorithms now leverage \emph{measurement-based uncomputation} (MBU), which replaces costly unitary $T$ gates with cheaper measurements and phase corrections. Current quantum programming frameworks can use measurement to uncompute specific gates such as Toffoli. No automatic transformation, however, accepts an arbitrary circuit whose ancillas are computed and uncomputed via the standard approach and converts the circuit to use MBU\@. Researchers instead apply MBU to individual circuit designs by hand, which limits algorithm development and compiler optimization. Such a transformation has not existed due to two fundamental unknowns: where MBU applies and which gates realize MBU for an arbitrary computation. To solve these, we first present a static analysis that identifies, for each ancilla qubit, each circuit position where measurement is sound --- subsuming basic assumptions that MBU only applies at the end of a circuit. Next, we present circuit transformations that soundly turn unitary uncomputation gates into efficient phase corrections after measurement --- generalizing rewrite rules from prior literature that are either limited to a single gate or not applicable to a general circuit. We present \textsf{MBUndo}, an integrated compiler pass that automatically converts circuits to measurement-based uncomputation. It requires no user annotations other than which qubits are ancillas, the same as needed by existing uncomputation synthesizers, and can enhance their output circuits. We evaluate \textsf{MBUndo} on 22 benchmarks to reveal \emph{T} gate reductions of ${>}36.5\%$ over uncomputation synthesizers.

papers.title_en: Finite attainment and efficient computation of regularized quantum channel relative entropy
papers.abstract_en: Quantum channel relative entropy can be nonadditive, making its regularization essential for asymptotic analysis. We study when the regularized value is attained at finite blocklength and how efficiently it can be approximated. For the first question, we establish a sharp dichotomy: the regularized value is either attained already at the single-copy level, implying additivity at every blocklength, or is never attained at any finite blocklength. Notably, a simple two-copy additivity test distinguishes between these alternatives for qubit channels and for channel pairs in arbitrary dimensions admitting an interior optimizer. We further show that both the interiority condition and finite nonattainment are generic, holding for almost every channel pair. For the second question, we establish explicit convergence rates for approximating the regularized channel relative entropy. For fixed channel dimensions, $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ channel copies suffice to approximate the regularized value to additive accuracy $\varepsilon$. Alternatively, a semidefinite hierarchy achieves the same accuracy at level $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$, yielding a certified polynomial-time approximation. Together, these results reveal the intriguing structure and generic behavior of regularized channel relative entropy, sharpening our understanding of both its analytical and computational aspects.

papers.title_en: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity
papers.abstract_en: Capacity-approaching quantum error correction faces a fundamental tension: the required parity-check matrices need to become increasingly dense, while practical decoding and syndrome extraction favor sparse, bounded-degree structures. Reconciling these competing requirements remains an important open problem in quantum code design. We construct Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code ensembles that approach the CSS rate over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding while retaining sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The construction separates parity-check density from graphical complexity: although capacity-approaching components may require dense parity-check matrices, they are represented by sparse concatenated factor graphs. We first study a construction combining low-density parity-check (LDPC) and low-density generator-matrix (LDGM) component codes and numerically analyze the average weight distributions of the resulting codes. Motivated by these results, we introduce a second construction based on concatenated LDPC and LDGM codes and generalized irregular repeat-accumulate (GIRA) codes. We derive bounds on the average weight distribution of the resulting sum ensemble and use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. Consequently, the proposed ensemble achieves rates arbitrarily close to the CSS hashing bound under separate bit- and phase-error correction, while maintaining bounded graphical complexity, thus providing a foundation for future iterative decoders and indirect syndrome-extraction architectures.

papers.title_en: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists
papers.abstract_en: AI scientists are expanding automated research across scientific domains, yet their ability to turn the scientific record into a foundation for autonomous discovery remains elusive. Here we uncover a fundamental barrier to this transition and demonstrate a route to overcome it in computational quantum science, where advances shape both what we can learn from complex quantum systems and what quantum computing can ultimately deliver. To identify this barrier, we introduce OmniQ, an expert-audited virtual research environment that converts published studies into executable reproduction tasks. Across 59 papers spanning classical simulation, quantum algorithms and quantum-property characterization, we systematically evaluate five agentic systems powered by large language models and six third-party agent harnesses. Our findings reveal that current AI scientists often fail to reproduce published results, exposing a fundamental mismatch between what scientific papers communicate and what autonomous agents require. By contrast, human expert intervention can turn these failures into successful reproductions, showing that the missing information can be identified and converted into reusable research experience. Guided by this observation, we develop Residual Agents (RA), a quantum-tailored self-improving AI scientist that distils externally verified workflow repairs into such experience. RA substantially improves research performance under fixed base models and limited adaptation budgets. For example, RA raises DeepSeek V4.1 Flash performance from 68% to 85%, matching Claude Code with Opus 5 at a third of its cost despite using a weaker base model. We integrate all reproduced results into an extensible platform built on the model context protocol, making verified research workflows directly accessible to AI scientists and allowing new scientific papers to be continuously incorporated.

papers.title_en: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
papers.abstract_en: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(Ω(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.

papers.title_en: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract_en: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.

papers.title_en: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform
papers.abstract_en: Most quantum circuit platforms focus on idealized circuit assembly and simulation, hiding hardware compilation, error identification, and variational model training behind black-box operations. QYANTRAM addresses this gap through an open platform comprising four subsystems, built around evidence-backed results and independent verification. Its staged compilation pipeline makes every transformation traceable, while the router publishes rejected SWAP candidates and their scores for transparent decision-making. Verification exploits inactive qubits remaining in the |0> state, reducing complexity from 2^N to 2^k for k active qubits. This mathematically exact reduction enables full pre-compilation verification on 127- and 156-qubit layouts, achieving approximately 10,000x speed-ups with execution times below one millisecond. The error identification engine exhaustively evaluates all Pauli error patterns without sampling, matching closed-form predictions within 2.8e-17. Its machine-learning engine achieves numerical agreement within 2.0e-15 of qiskit.quantum_info while training 25-50 times faster. The router introduces approximately 1.27x more SWAP gates than Qiskit's SABRE due to its omission of optimization, trading routing efficiency for complete decision transparency and traceability.

papers.title_en: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
papers.abstract_en: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound $\varepsilon$ on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of \textit{bad} seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce $δ$-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability $\left(\frac{\varepsilon}δ\right)^2$. This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of $k$ rounds except with failure probability $\big(\frac{(2k-1)\varepsilon}δ\big)^2$. Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.

papers.title_en: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
papers.abstract_en: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.

papers.title_en: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
papers.abstract_en: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate $τ=rd_2/d_1\geq 1$ as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. While the optimal bounds in the boundary regime ($τ=1$) and the away-from-boundary regime ($τ\geq 1+Ω(1)$) are now known, the precise behavior in the near-boundary regime ($1<τ<1+o(1)$) has remained unresolved. In this paper, we close this gap, thereby fully settling the query complexity of quantum channel tomography. Specifically, we show that the query complexity is - $Ω(rd_1d_2/\varepsilon^2)$ for diamond norm error $\varepsilon$, matching the upper bound by [MB26, CGO+26], - $Θ(d_1^2/\varepsilon+\min\{(τ-1)d_1^2,(τ-1)^2d_1^2d_2^2\}/\varepsilon^2)$ for Choi trace norm error $\varepsilon$. Our results reveal two qualitatively different forms of the Heisenberg-to-classical transition. For diamond norm tomography, the Heisenberg scaling disappears suddenly as soon as $τ$ leaves the boundary regime. In contrast, Choi trace norm tomography exhibits a gradual transition from Heisenberg to classical scaling as $τ$ moves from the boundary regime to the away-from-boundary regime.

papers.title_en: Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format
papers.abstract_en: We present a preconditioning pipeline that accelerates Tensor Train (TT) linear solvers for symmetric positive-definite problems. Extending the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, we construct a preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose. This formulation is positive semidefinite for any bond dimension and truncation, and definite whenever the factor is non-singular, satisfying the mathematical requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. We detail the construction of this preconditioner and its integration into Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG)-like linear solvers. Performance evaluations show consistent iteration reductions for anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems across various configurations, leading to net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned settings of time stepping schemes that can reuse the approximate inverses. These benchmarks were performed with the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl, which we also introduce in this work to provide out-of-the-box access to these preconditioned pipelines.

papers.title_en: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
papers.abstract_en: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) processes temporal information through quantum dynamics, but it remains unclear whether small QRC models can forecast real data competitively with classical models and whether their predictions survive the transfer from ideal simulation to noisy hardware. We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. Five reservoir candidates were selected and frozen using hardware-native interaction graphs, Trotterized Ising dynamics, memory and measurement-robustness criteria, circuit cost, and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out test days, the ideal candidates reached root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 5.66-6.12 claims/day, compared with 5.36 for ridge regression. For four of the five, the difference from ridge was not significant under a 95% block bootstrap, and their accuracy was comparable with classical recurrent and reservoir baselines. On the 156-qubit IBM Kingston processor, we ran 63 evaluations in 21 paired rounds, comparing hardware-aware, random-native, and Qiskit optimization level 1 layouts. Hardware-aware placement gave lower RMSE than Qiskit in every round, with a maximum transfer distortion of 7.59 claims/day (11.84 for Qiskit), and avoided the severe transfer failures seen for some random layouts. Most of the hardware distortion appeared as a systematic forecast shift, which a short hardware probe on training inputs detected before the test runs. Longer replay windows raised circuit cost without a consistent gain in forecasting accuracy or hardware transfer. Small QRC models can thus reach competitive accuracy on this task, and hardware-aware layout selection makes their transfer to IBM Kingston more consistent.

papers.title_en: Quantum tomography on Schwartz space
papers.abstract_en: In this work we show that standard results in quantum tomography, which are typically proven in the context of Hilbert spaces, can analogously be established in the theory of Schwartz spaces. In particular, we will see that quantum states are equivalently characterized by their Wigner function, the characteristic of their Wigner function, and the probability distributions for a family of linear combinations of position and momentum. Physically, the latter can be understood as the evolution of its probability distribution in position over time under, for example, free or harmonic evolution. The result is obtained with techniques that are more accessible to a physicist audience, and shows that, at least for tomography results, the full structure of Hilbert spaces is not necessary.

papers.title_en: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
papers.abstract_en: We prove propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. More precisely, we construct local representatives of evolved fermionic many-body interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth of order $d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ and suitable cell partitions. For the even Hamiltonian interaction $Φ_u$ and the even interaction $Ψ$ being evolved, we assume bounds, uniform in the site, on sums of term norms over finite supports $X$ containing a given site, with weights $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^a$ and $e^{κ|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$, respectively. Here $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, $0\le p\le a$, $κ$ is sufficiently large, and the Hamiltonian bound is uniform in time. We construct local representatives whose interaction norms with weight $e^{c(1+|t-s|)^{-b}|X|}(1+\operatorname{diam}X)^p$ grow at most polynomially in $|t-s|$, for suitable $c,b>0$. In particular, $p=a$ is allowed: the Hamiltonian need not decay faster than the interaction being evolved. The threshold $a>d_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is optimal in general: uniform polynomial time bounds at $p=a$ fail for $0<a\le d_{\mathrm{vol}}$, even for smooth time-dependent two-site interactions. Polynomial time growth permits integration against filters with sufficiently many finite absolute moments, including those used in quasi-adiabatic constructions and quantum belief propagation. We derive consequences for filtered interactions and the dynamics they generate, providing dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations, including gap stability, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally (LPPL), adiabatic theory, and response theory. All results also hold for quantum spin systems.

papers.title_en: Lee-Yang theorems for $q$-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK
papers.abstract_en:
We show that the vacuum partition function of the $q$-deformed oscillator 
\[ L_q(z):= \langle0|e^{zT_q}|0\rangle, \qquad T_q := \mathsf{a}_q + \mathsf{a}_q^* \]
 satisfies the Lee-Yang property, i.e., all zeros of $L_q$ lie on the imaginary line for all $q\in[-1, 1)$, proving the conjectures of Okuyama'23. Using the connection between $q$-deformed oscillators and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian in the doubly-scaled regime, we show that the annealed SYK partition function satisfies the Lee-Yang property in the thermodynamic limit, that is, all of its Fisher zeros are on the imaginary axis. As a result, we show that the quenched SYK partition function admits a zero-free strip of constant width with high probability, rigorously complementing the large$-k$ replica calculations of Zlokapa and Kiani'26. We show the imaginary-rootedness of $L_q$ by expressing $φ_q(z):= L_q(\mathbf{i} z)$ as a locally uniform limit of ``$q$-deformed'' matching polynomials and then showing that those $q$-deformed polynomials are real-rooted. This establishes that $φ_q$ is real-rooted, and in fact belongs to the \emph{Laguerre-Pólya} class. The real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials yields novel log-concavity relations on the \emph{$q$-deformed matching moments}
\[M_\ell(q):= \sum_{π\in\mathcal{P}_2(2\ell)}q^{\operatorname{cr}(π)}.\]
 We show the real-rootedness of the $q$-deformed polynomials by using the Touchard--Riordan formula to derive a partial differential equation relating their $q$-derivatives to their $z$-derivatives, and then analyzing the resulting motion of their roots.

papers.title_en: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
papers.abstract_en: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.

papers.title_en: Impact on Final-State Bulk Observables in Heavy-Ion Collisions from an Extended MC Glauber Model of Quantum Rotors
papers.abstract_en: Nuclear structure is closely connected to anisotropic flow in central heavy-ion collisions (HICs), so flow observables provide important probes for constraining nuclear deformation. Conventional Monte Carlo (MC) models typically describe deformed nuclei as classical rotors with definite orientations, whereas the ground states of even--even nuclei with $J=0$ are rotationally invariant. Motivated by the importance of rotational symmetry restoration, we systematically investigate symmetric collisions involving the representative even--even nuclei $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, $^{28}\mathrm{Si}$, $^{96}\mathrm{Ru}$, and $^{238}\mathrm{U}$ using an extended MC Glauber model that incorporates quantum superposition of nuclear orientations. In the final state, the quantum treatment suppresses elliptic flow $v_2\{2\}$, with the strongest effect observed in ultra-central Ne+Ne collisions. Quantum superposition further induces system-dependent changes in normalized symmetric cumulants and shifts the Pearson correlation between $v_2^2$ and $[p_T]$ toward the corresponding near-spherical reference values. Moreover, the quantum treatment modifies cross-system flow ratios and the U+U/Au+Au covariance ratio used experimentally to constrain nuclear deformation parameters. Our results suggest that the quantum-rotor treatment may affect the interpretation of nuclear structure information inffered from heavy-ion collision final-state observables.

papers.title_en: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV$^-$ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath
papers.abstract_en: The Hahn-echo time $T_2$ of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) ensembles in nitrogen-rich diamond follows the empirical relation $T_2\cdot$[N] = 160 $μ$s ppm, and this relation does not depend on the magnetic field between 2 and 30 mT. Cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations solve the spin dynamics exactly within small groups of spins. When they treat the Overhauser field of the surrounding P1 centres, that is, the field that these electron spins produce, as frozen, they overestimate $T_2$ at high field by up to a factor of two. This excess was recently attributed to additional dark defects. We show that the excess comes mostly from the frozen field. In our model the P1 centres outside each cluster flip-flop in pairs: two centres exchange their spin states and conserve their total $S_z$. Kinetic Monte Carlo generates these events at golden-rule rates, which follow from the dipolar Hamiltonian without adjustable parameters, and each cluster evolves in the resulting time-dependent field. This dynamical mean field lies between the static-mean-field and mean-field-free limits. For a $^{14}$N P1 bath it reduces $T_2\cdot$[N] at 30 mT from 264 $\pm$ 16 to 188 $\pm$ 12 $μ$s ppm and gives 167 $\pm$ 11 $μ$s ppm at 10 mT, 1.7 and 0.4 standard deviations from experiment, with no dark spins. When each centre jumps independently, $T_2\cdot$[N] is 147 $\pm$ 9 $μ$s ppm at 30 mT; the correlation of the flip-flop partners thus lengthens $T_2$ by 20-30 percent at high field. The Overhauser field is neither frozen nor averaged out by fast motion: 68-83 percent of its autocorrelation survives 200 $μ$s. At 2.5 mT, where the P1 electron and nucleus hybridise, $T_2$ stays below experiment for any choice of rates. Part of the field dependence therefore remains: $T_2$ rises by a factor 1.69 $\pm$ 0.07 instead of 2.15 $\pm$ 0.08 from 2.5 to 30 mT.

papers.title_en: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
papers.abstract_en: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re-enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schrödingerisation, which turns a non-unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the circuit, in one, two and three dimensions. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the common velocity-only damping mask. For the sponge the quantum analysis is sharp: recovery is exact on the whole non- negative half of the auxiliary axis at every time; that axis can be truncated periodically at a length set by the largest damping rate and the simulated time; and the success probability is a fixed constant, about 0.4, times the fraction of the energy not yet absorbed, with only one or two auxiliary qubits measured. On the circuit side, the damping step, which generic synthesis compiles into a number of controlled-NOT gates exponential in the number of qubits, factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

papers.title_en: Matching $ν$2HDM onto $ν$SMEFT up to one-loop accuracy
papers.abstract_en: The neutrinophilic two-Higgs-doublet model ($ν$2HDM) represents one of the most economical extensions of the Standard Model (SM) while still giving rise to a rich phenomenology. In this work, we carry out a full tree-level and one-loop matching of this ultraviolet completion onto the SM Effective Field Theory extended with right-handed neutrinos ($ν$SMEFT), including all operators up to mass dimension six. This is achieved by integrating out the heavy scalar doublet at a scale well above the electroweak scale. For the matching procedure, we employ the functional method in combination with the naive dimensional regularization and modified minimal subtraction schemes. After converting from the Green's basis to the minimal, non-redundant Warsaw-extended basis, the effects of high-scale new physics are encoded in the Wilson coefficients of both physical and evanescent operators in the $ν$SMEFT. These coefficients are given in terms of the $ν$2HDM parameters prior to spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our final expressions at the high-energy matching scale are provided as ancillary files on \href{https://github.com/dufewe/v2HDM-to-vSMEFT}{GitHub}. This setup forms the foundation for forthcoming systematic and global analyses of the $ν$2HDM parameter space using effective field theory techniques.

papers.title_en: Quantum teleportation using photon-added two-mode squeezed Fock states: A comparison with photon-subtracted counterparts
papers.abstract_en: Quantum state engineering frequently employs non-Gaussian operations, particularly photon addition and subtraction, to tailor and improve the nonclassical characteristics of quantum states. We investigate how photon addition to a two-mode squeezed Fock state (TMSFS) influences its performance in the Braunstein-Kimble quantum teleportation protocol. We obtain the Wigner characteristic function of the photon-added TMSFS (PA-TMSFS) and evaluate the corresponding teleportation fidelities for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian input states. We further compare the teleportation performance of PA-TMSFS with that of its photon-subtracted counterpart by accessing their fidelity enhancements over the parent TMSFS and considering the probabilistic nature of both the operations. Our results demonstrate that photon subtraction provides superior teleportation performance compared with photon addition, with this advantage becoming more pronounced when the success probabilities of the corresponding non-Gaussian operations are considered. In particular, the symmetric $(1,1)$ photon subtraction yields the optimal trade-off between teleportation fidelity and success probability among the configurations investigated. These findings highlight that photon subtraction retains its advantage even when the underlying entangled resource is already non-Gaussian.

papers.title_en: On-shell constituent approach to the light-front partonic energy-momentum tensor
papers.abstract_en: The forward matrix elements of the energy-momentum tensor in momentum space, parameterized by gravitational transverse-momentum distributions (TMDs), provide a microscopic window into hadronic mechanical structure. While the longitudinal and transverse columns match to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, the light-front minus column involves the unintegrated parton energy $k^-$, leaving this sector undetermined in general quantum chromodynamics. Working within relativistic light-front constituent frameworks where active quarks are modeled as effective on-shell quasiparticles, we show that this energy factorizes algebraically. This establishes a closed matching relating all 32 gravitational TMDs to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, including target polarization and T-odd final-state interactions. This completion provides access to the light-front energy density and its transverse Sivers dipole distortion, demonstrates the local equivalence between convective energy and momentum transport velocities, and determines the longitudinal normal stress. Comparing longitudinal and transverse stresses yields a boost-invariant anisotropy ratio that charts the mechanical crossover from collinear confinement dominance to transverse isotropic balance. While formulated within the constituent approximation, these results offer baseline insights into the three-dimensional continuum mechanics of the nucleon.

papers.title_en: Evaluation of $2νββ$ decay nuclear matrix elements using Lanczos techniques preserving Gamow-Teller strengths from both parent and daughter nuclei
papers.abstract_en: We present two efficient shell-model approaches for calculating nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) for two-neutrino double-beta ($2νββ$) decay and two-neutrino double-electron capture ($2ν$ECEC), based on the Lanczos strength-function and block-Lanczos techniques. The dual-sided Lanczos strength-function (DLSF) and block-Lanczos strength-function (BLSF) methods avoid the explicit calculation of a complete set of exact intermediate $1^+$ eigenstates and yield fully converged NMEs with a relatively small number of iterations starting from Gamow--Teller (GT) doorway states. Both methods simultaneously preserve the total GT strengths associated with the initial and final nuclei. We benchmark the methods for $^{48}$Ca in the $fp$ shell and apply them to candidates in different mass regions, including $^{58}$Ni, $^{76}$Ge, and $^{130}$Te. For $^{48}$Ca, a calculation allowing cross-shell excitations of up to $2\hbarω$ in the $sdpf$ model space yields a $2νββ$ NME closer to the experimental estimate than the result obtained in the $fp$ shell. For $^{58}$Ni, we present, to our knowledge, the first shell-model calculation of the $2νβ^+$EC/$2ν$ECEC NME. Comparison with the current experimental upper limit on the NME indicates the need for a more sensitive measurement of the $2νβ^+$EC half-life. As an independent validation, the energy-denominator-free sums obtained with the proposed methods are compared with the corresponding double-GT matrix elements calculated directly between the initial and final ground states. Their agreement demonstrates that the methods correctly recover the complete energy-denominator-free intermediate-state sums.

papers.title_en: Barycentric programming: Classical realization of programs for universal quantum processors
papers.abstract_en: A programmable quantum processor implements a target unitary using information stored in a classical or quantum program register. For arbitrary unitaries in $\mathrm{SU}(d)$, quantum programs attain the optimal leading-order memory cost, whereas deterministic classical rounding requires twice as much memory for the same diamond-distance error. We show that this gap disappears when classical randomization is allowed. We introduce barycentric programming, which stores the label of a unitary randomly selected from a finite set, with probabilities chosen so that first-order approximation errors cancel in the averaged unitary channel. Consequently, the diamond-distance error scales quadratically with the discretization spacing. For any $ν$-parameter family of unitaries forming a compact, smooth manifold without boundary, this method achieves error $\varepsilon$ using only $(ν/2)\log_2(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)$ classical bits. We also prove a matching lower bound for arbitrary quantum programs, determining the optimal leading-order program size for general unitary families. Thus, classical randomization achieves the optimal scaling $(ν/2+o(1))\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$ without requiring coherent quantum memory.

papers.title_en: Nearly Transform-Limited Pulse-Like Temporal and Narrowband Spectral Responses in Sum-Frequency Generation from Bright Twin Beams
papers.abstract_en: We simultaneously characterize the temporal and spectral responses of the coherent component in bright twin beams using a spectrally resolved, delay-dependent sum-frequency generation (SFG) measurement. The measured temporal-correlation width is 0.138 ps, close to the transform-limited value of 0.126 ps estimated from the measured twin-beam spectrum.The observed spectral-correlation width is 0.176 rad/ps and is limited by the spectrometer resolution. The corresponding time-frequency width product is 0.0243, far below the value of 1 for SFG between two independent transform-limited Gaussian pulses.

papers.title_en: Logarithmic Bias of Zero-Noise Extrapolation under 1/f Noise
papers.abstract_en: Zero-noise extrapolation estimates ideal quantum observables by amplifying noise and extrapolating the measured response. Its accuracy depends on whether the extrapolation model captures the physical effect of amplification, including correlations between repeated operations. Here we derive the response of complete multiqubit gate folding in the simultaneous presence of time-local Markovian noise and stationary finite-band 1/f noise. An ordered circuit kernel couples the observable to noise memory; exact block counting shows how folding samples correlations at increasing time separations. The resulting response contains an r^2 ln r coordinate, with a coefficient fixed by the noise spectrum and the integrated forward-inverse control response. Ordinary polynomial Richardson extrapolation leaves a calculable contribution from this coordinate; the three-node rule (1,3,5) retains 2.73 theta. We construct response-matched extrapolation, including a log-domain implementation, that cancels this contribution at the retained order. Explicit bounds separate the remaining control-shape, finite-band, higher-order, and native-offset errors. The theory applies to arbitrary finite multiqubit circuits within the stated control and noise model, and distinguishes removal of memory-induced bias from an unconditional guarantee of the ideal intercept. Single- and ten-qubit numerical examples illustrate the predicted correction and its response dependence.

papers.title_en: Track reconstruction with ACTAR TPC: a transfer-reaction use case
papers.abstract_en: A unified framework for track reconstruction in the ACTAR Time Projection Chamber (ACTAR TPC) is presented, designed to address the specific challenges of direct-reaction and resonance-elastic scattering experiments involving exotic nuclei. The actroot software package enables efficient semi-online analysis by integrating a continuity-based clustering algorithm followed by a modular filtering procedure to reduce noise, delta-electron contamination, and track fragmentation. The software was benchmarked with experimental data taken with a secondary 20O beam delivered by the LISE3 spectrometer at GANIL. The algorithm achieves reconstruction efficiencies exceeding 90% across various event topologies. The system provides accurate particle identification and reaction-point determination, facilitating the extraction of key physical observables. These results demonstrate the framework's suitability for its application to direct reaction experiments in cubic active-target TPCs without magnetic fields.

papers.title_en: Strong vertex $N N ρ$ in dense medium
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the strong coupling form factors associated with the $NNρ$ interaction vertex in nuclear matter using the QCD sum rule framework. These form factors are calculated incorporating the in-medium modifications of the relevant condensates and operators into the operator product expansion (OPE) for the first time. We analyze the behavior of the strong form factors as functions of the momentum transfer squared and density of medium and evaluate the corresponding strong couplings at the on-shell point of the $ρ$ meson at nuclear saturation density. Then we extend the analyses to get information at higher densities. Our results provide complementary information on the in-medium $NNρ$ interaction and may be useful for phenomenological, experimental and observational studies of dense hadronic matter.

papers.title_en: Performance analysis of cat and GKP breeding protocols with squeezed single-photon input
papers.abstract_en: Homodyne breeding is a promising optical route for generating large cat states and Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) grid states, using readily available squeezed-cat states as inputs. We analyze the performance of protocols, using squeezed single-photon seeds, $\hat{S}(r)\ket{1}$, as squeezed-cat resources and propagating them through the same cat-to-GKP breeding pipeline. For a symmetric tree with $N=2^{m_1}$ seeds, the heralded resource state reduces to a state with a polynomial-Gaussian wavefunction controlled by a single effective width, achieving near-unit fidelity with the desired cat resource state. Our analysis yields closed-form even-cat fidelities and an inverse-design rule for the seed squeezing. We apply these resources to GKP breeding, and find a large overlap with a practical GKP state. We also investigate the effects of practical imperfections, including finite homodyne acceptance windows and photon loss. This study shows that squeezed single-photon inputs provide a viable resource assignment for homodyne cat and GKP breeding, replacing the demanding requirement for high-resolution photon-number-resolving heralding with an on-demand single-photon source.

papers.title_en: Search for dark photon dark matter near $\mathbf{1\,meV}$ using a superconducting mixer
papers.abstract_en: We demonstrate the use of a superconducting mixer for direct searches for dark photon dark matter (DPDM) in the meV mass range. DPDM couples to the ordinary electromagnetic field through kinetic mixing with a coupling constant $χ$ and can convert into ordinary photons at the surface of a metal plate. For DPDM masses of 1 meV, the conversion photons have frequencies of around 240 GHz. At such frequencies, superconducting mixers enable low-noise spectroscopic measurements. We performed a direct search for DPDM in the mass range 1.0047578-1.0047598 meV, corresponding to the frequency range 242.94935-242.94983 GHz, using approximately one hour of data obtained with a cryogenic millimeter-wave receiver based on a superconducting mixer. No significant excess was found, and we set upper limits of $χ< (1.6\text{-}1.9)\times10^{-9}$ at the 95% confidence level. These limits are comparable to existing constraints from solar dark photons. By applying this method, we plan to extend the search to the wider mass range of 0.7-1.1 meV, corresponding to 170-260 GHz, with improved sensitivity.

papers.title_en: Numerical Study of Two-Frequency Heating in ECR Ion Source
papers.abstract_en: The two-frequency heating (TFH) method is widely used to improve the performance of electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) ion sources, yet its physical mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. In this work, the TFH regime in the DECRIS-PM ECR ion source is studied numerically using the NAM-ECRIS code. Single-frequency heating at 14.51 GHz (500 W) is compared to two-frequency heating at 14.51 GHz and 13 GHz (450 W + 50 W) at equal total power. It is found that while the global plasma parameters remain largely unchanged, the peak density of highly anisotropic electrons (E > 1 keV, Vperp/Vlong > 10) decreases by ~20% and their distribution broadens radially in the TFH regime. This reduction in electron anisotropy is attributed to the randomizing effect of the lower-frequency wave on electron gyromotion, which suppresses plasma micro-instabilities and leads to improved ion production.

papers.title_en: Coulomb Blockade in a One-Dimensional Array of Strong Josephson Junctions
papers.abstract_en: We measure current across a voltage-biased, long array of Josephson junctions. Current-voltage characteristics do not reveal any critical current and instead display the presence of threshold voltage and finite activation energy, consistent with the Coulomb blockade. However, the respective energy scale is well below the value prescribed by a single-island geometric capacitances. We explain it by strong quantum fluctuations of charge associated with a large value of Josephson energy, $E_J\gg E_C$, where $E_C$ is the charging energy associated with the inter-island capacitance. Comparison between the data and theory points to an exponential (in parameter $E_J/E_C$) suppression of the threshold. We achieve a quantitative agreement with theory by accounting for charge-$e$ solitons associated with the quasiparticles entering the array from its leads. This scenario however underestimates the current below threshold in comparison with the experiment.

papers.title_en: Entanglement inference from quantum erasure and path discrimination
papers.abstract_en: Fringes recovered by conditioning on quantum-eraser outcomes do not, by themselves, establish entanglement. We determine the minimum entanglement compatible with recorded eraser data when the preparation may be mixed, distinguishing these data from independently determined optimal which-path distinguishabilities and additional joint measurement outcomes. For noisy Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) preparations, explicit compatible states establish sharp entanglement-depth thresholds and show how parity information strengthens certification. A matching converse establishes the exact threshold for two complete Pauli-outcome distributions.
